title: Your Highness, Stop Holding Back, You've Crushed Your Prayer Beads
author: Caomei Bu Shi Zheme Chi Da
synopsis:
Adapted short drama "Crossing the Abyss of Dust" currently open for reservation.

[True master-manipulator sea-mariner beauty × paranoid, crazy, ascetic crown prince, 1v1, male lead goes crazy and falls in love first, super sweet and high flirt]

"I cultivate Buddhism and keep away from women."

"Then what was that pressing against this subject last night... Your Highness?"

Transmigrated into the Marquis's legitimate daughter who was pua-ed to death, Su Yaoyao looked at her plump, seductive figure in the mirror and smiled.

The original owner was truly wasting heaven's gift; this waist is slim and legs are long, with full breasts, yet she was bound so tightly her complexion turned sallow, and she was even called "fat" by her fiance, the second prince?

She is a max-level sea-mariner! Men? There are only men she doesn't want to flirt with, none she can't catch.

Ripping off the chest binder, she returned as an earthly siren.

She turned around and started flirting with the scumbag's older brother, the legendary pure and desireless crown prince and Buddhist devotee.

Everyone said the crown prince kept away from women and would sooner or later convert to Buddhism.

Yet in the dim ancestral hall, he pinned her against the scriptural texts, the prayer beads pressing against her snow-white skin, his breathing burning hot:

"Su Yaoyao, is this what you want?"

She hooked his lapel with an alluring smile,

"Your Highness's Buddha saves all sentient beings, but can he save himself?"

Later, the scumbag second prince regretted to tears and begged for reconciliation. Leaning in the crown prince's embrace, she played with the prayer beads nonchalantly:

"Too late, now... call me sister-in-law."

His Highness the aloof Buddhist prince murmured beside her ear, paranoid yet affectionate:

"Yaoyao, if there is a hell with you, I gladly welcome it."

The aloof Buddhist prince sinks into depravity while fully awake.

chapters.title: The Buddhist Prince Breaks His Vows, the Sea-Mariner Reborn
chapters.content:
"...Your Highness, your prayer beads are pressing against me."

The voice was coquettish, carrying pants, sounding exceptionally alluring in the dim ancestral hall.

Crown Prince Xiao Chenyuan's well-articulated fingers were tangled with that string of sandalwood prayer beads, beneath his palm was half-undressed female attire, revealing plump, snow-white skin.

Su Yaoyao looked up at him, her alluring eyes like silk, her gaze shifting with not a shred of the daytime's timidity and shyness.

With a snap, the prayer beads broke.

Xiao Chenyuan's breathing also fell into disorder.

He lowered his eyelashes, candlelight casting shadows on his refined profile, his thin lips parting slightly:

"Knowing it presses against you, why not hide?"

His tone was calm, just as untroubled as when he lectured on scriptures in the ancestral hall, yet his hand continued to stroke the snow-white of her collarline.

Su Yaoyao gave a light laugh, not hiding at all, but instead pressing further into his palm.

"Why should this subject hide? Has Your Highness not already... broken your vows?"

Before her voice faded, her waist was suddenly caught by a force, and in a spinning blur, she was pinned beneath Xiao Chenyuan.

He gazed down at her from above, those eyes that ordinarily held only Buddhist scriptures and all living beings now reflecting her flushed face tinged with passion.

"Su Yaoyao," he called her full name, his voice deep,

"You are my second brother's fiancee..."

"Him?"

"Does he even deserve it?" Su Yaoyao let out a soft chuckle, as if hearing the most ridiculous joke in the world.

Then she reached out boneless hands to hook around Xiao Chenyuan's neck, pulling him closer,

"However... even if he is... so what?"

Su Yaoyao leaned close to his earlobe, nibbling it lightly, her breath sweet like orchid,

"Does Your Highness not like this body of mine?"

Xiao Chenyuan's gaze darkened.

How could he not like it?

On the day of their first encounter at the palace banquet, this future sister-in-law of his had still looked like a frail willow in the wind, wrapped in layers of skirts, sallow-faced, following meekly behind his second brother like a flower that had lost its water.

Yet in merely a month, she seemed completely reborn.

Her waist remained slender, but no longer with a sickly, forced thinness; her chest was full and abundant, no longer bound layer upon layer by cloth strips;

Her complexion was rosy, her shifting gaze bright, and even her lips were so vivid they made it impossible to look away.

The memory cut off abruptly because the woman beneath him moved restlessly.

Xiao Chenyuan's breathing hitched, and he reached out to press her moving wrist,

"Don't move. Move again, and I cannot guarantee... what will happen next..."

Su Yaoyao exuded alluring charm, "Your Highness has cultivated Buddhism for many years..."

"Do you know what 'If I do not enter hell, who will?' means?"

Xiao Chenyuan gazed at her for a long time before suddenly leaning down to whisper in her ear:

"If this is hell, I would have gladly descended into it for you long ago."

The moment the words fell, an eager kiss landed, and a large hand slipped into her bodice.

The prayer beads fell with a "pat," scattering all over the floor.

If the Su Yaoyao of three months ago had seen this scene, she probably would have been scared to death all over again.

After all, back then, the entire capital knew that Su Yaoyao, the legitimate daughter of the Marquis of Yongning, was the second prince's disliked fiancee, a laughingstock who bound her chest due to excessive plumpness and starved herself until she was sallow and haggard.

"Older sister, is your dress today... a bit tight?" Half-sister Su Yun'er pinched her handkerchief, covering her smile, her gaze full of mockery,

"I'm running out of breath just looking at you."

Su Yaoyao, or rather, the original Su Yaoyao, kept her head down, her fingers desperately twisting the corner of her dress.

Today was her coming-of-age banquet.

She had deliberately worn a lotus-pink ruqun, but what should have been full breasts were forcefully squeezed out of shape, looking out of place.

"I-I'll change into another one next time..." Her voice grew quieter and quieter.

"Next time?" Second Prince Xiao Chiming nearby sneered aloud, "Su Yaoyao, what difference does it make what you wear? Sallow complexion, devoid of decorum, and these breasts... Hmph, shameless!"

Su Yaoyao's face turned pale.

She wasn't fat at all, it was just this chest...

The concubine-mother had said her appearance was disgraceful, telling her to eat only one meal a day, bind her chest tightly, and keep her chest hunched even when walking.

She obediently followed, starving until she was dizzy and bruised by the bindings, yet this figure... seemed to deliberately oppose her.

"Second Prince," she mustered the courage to look up at her nominal fiance, "We, we are betrothed..."

"Betrothed?" Xiao Chiming laughed as if hearing a huge joke, pulling Su Yun'er into his arms by the shoulder,

"If not for the Empress and your maternal grandfather, this prince would find even looking at you disgusting!"

Su Yun'er timely reddened her eyes, timidly tugging his sleeve: "Your Highness, don't say that... Sister must be feeling so hurt..."

"She hurt? Does she even deserve to feel hurt?" Xiao Chiming spat, "Still, our Yun'er is better, as graceful as a willow in the wind, the true beauty in my heart."

Su Yun'er snuggled into Xiao Yu's embrace, her voice dripping with sweetness, "Sister, don't blame His Highness either. If you want to blame someone, blame this body of yours... for being too, too plump. These days, which noble young master likes this kind?"

The hall of guests covered their mouths and chuckled lowly.

She opened her mouth, wanting to argue.

But long-term oppression made even breathing difficult, let alone talking back.

She only felt darkness before her eyes.

Before losing consciousness, the last thing she heard was Xiao Chiming's impatient voice:

"Fainting again? Su Yaoyao, what else can you do besides this trick?"

The original owner was already frail, and after being humiliated like this in public, she couldn't catch her breath and was literally angered to death.

Inside Su Yaoyao's boudoir.

Opening her eyes once more, the shell had been replaced by a sea-mariner who had transmigrated from the modern entertainment circle, a top-tier player who had slept with top idols, flirted with CEO tycoons, passed through thousands of bushes without a single leaf sticking to her.

Su Yaoyao absorbed the aggrieved and cowardly memories that didn't belong to her in her brain.

Her chest felt stuffy and suffocating.

Subconsciously, she reached out and gave a yank.

"Rip..."

The ridiculously thick chest-binding cloth tied around her chest split apart at the sound.

Instantly.

The whole world felt fresh.

She felt like she had come back to life.

Propring herself up to a sitting position, she looked down.

Then, her eyes lit up.

"What a waste of heaven's gifts!!!"

This... what kind of divine, wonderful figure is this!

Her waist is absurdly slim, and her chest...

Magnificent waves!

As for this face, although somewhat sallow due to long-term malnutrition, the foundation is supreme.

Big eyes, high bridge of nose, pouty lips.

If she takes good care of this, she will definitely be a breathtaking stunner!

"With this body and appearance, in modern times, how many people would throw fortunes at plastic surgery just to get it? And you ruined it like this?"

Su Yaoyao felt grief-stricken.

"Original owner, oh original owner, you were begging for food while sitting on a gold mine. You held a royal flush and played it into a complete disaster?"

"Pua-ed to death by a green tea half-sister and a blind scumbag?"

"Do you treat this top-tier hardware justice?"

After scolding, she felt something was amiss.

The dead are the greatest.

Now that she occupied someone else's body and was still scolding her, it wasn't very kind.

"Fine, you silly girl."

Su Yaoyao patted her face and quickly calmed down.

"For the sake of this stunning skin, older sister will avenge you."

"As for those who looked down on you..."

Looking at the person in the mirror, she slowly curved her lips into an effortless smile belonging to a master sea-mariner.

"I will make them kneel down one by one, and watch just how beautiful this body of yours really is."

"Miss! Are you awake? The palace sent an invitation, saying His Highness the Crown Prince has returned..."

Outside the door came the eager voice of the maid Chuntao, accompanied by hurried footsteps.

chapters.title: Cold and Aloof Buddha-like Man? I Love It Most
chapters.content:
The door was pushed open, and a round-faced maid came in holding an invitation. Seeing Su Yaoyao sitting there, she was first overjoyed.

"Miss, you're awake! That's wonderful..."

Immediately, her gaze landed on Su Yaoyao...

Her young mistress was sitting before the dressing table with just an outer robe draped over her shoulders. The curves of her figure were breathtakingly stunning, and her waist was shockingly slender.

That pair of voluptuous breasts, suppressed for years, were now proudly upright, so fair and dazzling that they almost blinded her...

"M-Miss!" Chuntao nearly dropped the invitation, her face instantly turning beet red. "How, how could you take off your chest binder..."

"It was so tight I couldn't breathe. Was it supposed to choke me to death?" Su Yaoyao lazily lifted the heavy strip of binding cloth with an expression of disdain.

Chuntao stamped her feet in anxiety. "If the Concubine finds out about this, she'll say you're... you're lacking in modesty again..."

"Lacking in modesty?" Su Yaoyao gave her a gentle smile.

That smile left Chuntao stunned.

Her mistress's face was still the same face, but her gaze... was different.

In the past, when the young mistress looked at people, she would always dodge their eyes, terrified of saying a single wrong word.

But now, those apricot eyes rippled with light, bright and sparkling, carrying even a hint of... an indescribable, alluring charm...

"Chuntao."

Su Yaoyao suddenly called out to her, her voice softening a bit. "You're the one my mother left behind, right?"

Chuntao's eyes grew hot. "Yes, this servant was brought back from the Madam's maiden family. On her deathbed, Madam instructed me to take good care of the Miss..."

"Then listen well."

Su Yaoyao looked at her earnestly.

"Starting today, I am not binding my chest. I won't miss a single bite of food. My, Su Yaoyao's, figure is not for others to gossip about."

"But Miss, the Second Prince... doesn't like that..."

"The Second Prince?" Su Yaoyao stood up, carrying an indescribable allure and mockery.

"What is he?"

Chuntao was completely dumbfounded. Didn't the Miss care the most about the Second Prince's opinion in the past?

She suddenly remembered the expressions on the faces of the Second Prince and Su Yun'er after the young mistress fainted yesterday, and thought of all the grievances the Miss had suffered over the years.

A rush of heat surged to her head, and Chuntao nodded heavily. "This servant will listen to the Miss!"

"Good girl." Su Yaoyao smiled, her radiance making Chuntao stare in a daze once again.

"You said just now that an invitation has arrived from the palace?"

Su Yaoyao picked up a comb, leisurely brushing her somewhat dry, long hair.

"Ah... Yes, yes!" Chuntao snapped back to her senses and handed over the invitation she was holding.

"It says that three days from now, the Empress will host a banquet in the palace to welcome His Royal Highness the Crown Prince back to the capital. All eligible... young ladies from various mansions must attend."

She paused and added in a small voice,

"In past years, the Concubine used your poor health as an excuse to decline, but this time Her Majesty named you specifically..."

Su Yaoyao took the invitation, her fingertips gliding over the words "Crown Prince Xiao Chenyuan" written on it.

The memories belonging to the original owner surged in her mind...

Information about that Crown Prince was pitifully scarce. She only knew he was the legitimate son of the late Empress, raised since childhood by the current Empress, who was Su Yaoyao's maternal aunt. However, he was infatuated with Buddhism, spent year-round in solitary cultivation outside, had a cold and aloof temperament, kept his distance from women, and remained unmarried past the age of twenty.

It seemed her Empress aunt was growing anxious, wanting to use the welcome banquet as a disguised bride-selection event.

"Help me prepare a bath." She put down the invitation and walked toward the wardrobe.

Chuntao quickly acknowledged the order, but hesitated. "Miss, are you really going? Your health... hasn't fully recovered yet, and besides..."

She looked at Su Yaoyao's seductive charm that couldn't be hidden even beneath an outer robe, and her face turned red again. "And if you go looking like this, won't it..."

"Won't it be too flashy?" Su Yaoyao finished for her, pulling open the wardrobe with a swish.

Then, silence.

Inside the closet, everything was a dull, dusty gray.

The fabric was decent enough, but the style... couldn't be any more old-fashioned.

"These were all chosen by the Concubine... The Concubine said that with the Miss's figure... wearing these would make you look steady and unobtrusive..." Chuntao's voice grew softer and softer.

"Steady?" Su Yaoyao casually picked up a ruqun and sneered. "Ha, she certainly knows how to pick."

That concubine of the original owner truly mastered the art of "concealing needles in silk"using the ugliest clothes to ruin a fine beauty into a country bumpkin.

"Throw all of these away. Not a single one stays."

"Th-throw them away?" Chuntao's eyes widened.

Su Yaoyao turned around, sat before the dressing table, and examined her sallow complexion in the bronze mirror.

"Chuntao, tell me the truth, do you think how I looked before was pretty?"

Chuntao opened her mouth, and her eyes suddenly reddened.

She dropped to her knees with a thud.

"Miss... y-you were never supposed to look like that! Back then, Madam was the number one beauty in the capital, and when you were little, you were as cute as carved jade, who didn't praise you? But ever since Madam passed away and the Concubine took charge, she always said this and that was wrong with you..."

"Get up." Su Yaoyao reached out to help her up.

"Since you know it wasn't supposed to be like that, listen to me from now on."

"Yes!" Chuntao wiped away her tears. "B-but Miss, you're going to enter the palace for the banquet soon. What will you do without clothes..."

"Then we'll make new ones on the spot!"

Su Yaoyao sat down at the desk, picked up brush and paper...

And simply sketched out a draft for a dress.

The lines were clean and clear, without any redundant flashy decorations, yet subtly designed around the chest and waist, accentuating her curves without appearing frivolous.

"According to this pattern, find the best tailor."

Chuntao took the sketch, her eyes going wide. "This; this style... This servant has never seen it before..."

"Just make it according to this."

Of course, Su Yaoyao wouldn't say she specifically learned this in her past life just to flirt with a haute couture fashion designer.

Su Yaoyao pulled out another sheet of paper and began writing a list. "Also, go get these things ready."

Chuntao leaned in to look.

The paper read:

Rose water, milk, pearl powder, honey...

More than a dozen items in total.

"Miss, what are these..."

"To apply to my face." Su Yaoyao touched her still somewhat sallow cheeks.

This body had an exceptional foundation, but due to long-term malnutrition, her skin was sallow and dry, and her hair was brittle.

It didn't matter.

She had struggled and survived in the entertainment industry; what beauty secrets had she not used? In three days, she could still nurture this body back to being radiant and tender.

As for her figure...

Su Yaoyao looked down at the bursting, full curves at her chest, a curve hooking at the corner of her lips.

The original owner was truly a fool.

This body was born to shine brilliantly; why should it be hidden away?

"Oh, right," she finished writing the last stroke and looked up. "Where is the dowry list left by my mother?"

Chuntao's expression changed. "W-with the Concubine... Miss, why are you asking about this?"

Su Yaoyao's tone was flat. "I've come of age; it's time to take it back."

Chuntao's palms broke out in a sweat. "B-but the Concubine's side... I'm afraid..."

"That's not up to her!" Su Yaoyao's gaze flashed. "My maternal grandfather's family, the Grand Tutor's Mansion, has there been any movement from them recently?"

Chuntao was stunned. "They sent some supplements the other day, but the Concubine intercepted them..."

"Hah." Su Yaoyao sneered.

"Next time someone from the Grand Tutor's Mansion comes, invite them straight to my quarters," she said indifferently.

"Also, I'll write a letter later and have someone sent to my grandfather's place."

The towering tree of the Grand Tutor's Mansion, the original owner actually listened to that concubine and cut off contact for all these years?!

She wasn't the original owner, some soft bun to be easily manipulated. She had to firmly cling to her family's towering tree no matter what.

She paused and added, "Right, go and find out where His Royal Highness the Crown Prince usually goes after returning to the palace."

Chuntao was startled. "The Crown Prince? Why is the Miss asking about this?"

Su Yaoyao looked into the bronze mirror, tucking a stray strand of hair behind her ear. The reflection's eyes shifted fluidly, overflowing with allure.

"Naturally... to have a chance encounter."

"B-but the Miss still has a betrothal with the Second Prince..."

"Betrothal?" Su Yaoyao scoffed.

"It won't exist much longer."

Watching her mistress's retreating back, Chuntao suddenly felt that her young mistress was glowing all over.

It was a kind of unrestrained and vibrant radiance she had never seen on any noble lady in the capital.

"What are you standing around for?" Su Yaoyao looked back at her. "Go."

"Y-yes!"

Chuntao hurried out clutching the list and her overwhelming shock.

The room grew quiet.

Su Yaoyao's fingertips traced the words "Eastern Palace" on the invitation.

Crown Prince Xiao Chenyuan...

"A cold and aloof Buddha-like man..."

She curled her lips, her fingertips lightly tracing the handwriting on the invitation.

"I love it most."

She looked at her voluptuous figure in the mirror.

The more abstinent a person is... the more indulgent they become...

As she was thinking this, footsteps suddenly sounded outside.

Immediately after, a dainty voice rang out: "Is elder sister awake? Younger sister specially brewed some ginseng soup to come see you..."

chapters.title: The Little White Lotus Still Wants to Fight Me
chapters.content:
It was her concubine-born younger sister, Su Yun'er.

A trace of disgust flashed in the depths of Su Yaoyao's eyes.

She quickly pulled another outer robe from the wardrobe and draped it over herself, although she wasn't binding her chest anymore, now wasn't the time for a full showdown.

Su Yun'er walked in with a small tureen, smiling brightly.

Only that smile froze the moment her gaze touched Su Yaoyao.

The Su Yaoyao before her had simply draped an outer robe over herself, her long hair uncombed, yet that figure...

Without the layers of restriction from the binding cloth, even through the clothing, one could see breathtaking rises and falls.

Especially that waist, so slender it seemed as though it would snap with a single bend.

Clearly the simplest attire, arguably even casual, yet it possessed... an indescribable lazy allure.

Su Yun'er's fingers tightened around the tray, and that uncomfortable sourness in her heart bubbled up again.

This good-for-nothing... How is it that overnight, she seemed to have peeled off that dusty shell, revealing the scorching light inside?

And that figure... Didn't she bind her chest and starve herself every single day?

Yet she quickly adjusted her expression, donning her habitual vulnerability. "It's good that elder sister is awake; younger sister was worried all night. I specially had the kitchen brew some ginseng soup, which is best for restoring qi."

She placed the tureen on the table, her gaze seemingly accidentally sweeping over the pile of chest-binding cloth on the floor. A trace of disdain flashed in her eyes, but her tone grew even more "concerned":

"Why did elder sister... take that off? Is your health unwell again, or..."

She covered her lips, lowering her voice, "Or is it because of what the Second Prince said yesterday that you're hurting inside?"

She waited for Su Yaoyao to lower her head and twist her fingers or turn red-eyed, just like usual.

But Su Yaoyao merely lifted her eyes, looked at her, and smiled.

It was a faint smile, carrying a hint of... a playful interest Su Yun'er couldn't understand.

"Younger sister's ginseng soup must have been simmered for quite a while?" Su Yaoyao didn't take up her thread, pointing instead at the tureen of soup. "Judging by the clear broth, did you use premium old ginseng rootlets?"

Su Yun'er was startled and instinctively nodded. "Yes, it's top-grade old ginseng rootlets..."

"What a pity." Su Yaoyao sighed, shaking her head.

"Though the broth is clear, it's made from the absolute lowest-tier scrap ginseng clippings. To think younger sister took it out... still thinking it's top-grade old ginseng... Alas! I can't blame younger sister either... I suppose you haven't seen many fine objects."

Su Yun'er's face turned white as a sheet. "You!"

Then suddenly remembering something, she quickly steadied her expression. "Elder sister! I; I had good intentions..."

"Indeed, good intentions~" Su Yaoyao nodded, her tone still calm.

At that moment, a little maid walked in carrying a midday meal.

Simple dishes were set on the table: a bowl of clear soup floating a few vegetable leaves, and two rock-hard, grayish coarse-flour steamed buns.

At the sight of this food, Chuntao's expression turned ugly.

This was even worse than what the Miss usually ate!

Su Yaoyao laughed in anger.

"The Concubine really went to great lengths." She looked up at Su Yun'er, whose expression had yet to recover.

"My illness hasn't fully healed, and you give me this to eat? Even the lowest-tier coarse-cleaning maids in the mansion would find these buns too hard to bite into, I'm afraid?"

Su Yun'er forced out a smile. "Elder sister is misunderstanding. The Concubine thought that since elder sister received... a blow yesterday, you might not have an appetite. Besides, didn't elder sister always want to be slimmer to win the Second Prince's favor..."

"Win his favor?" Su Yaoyao interrupted, dropping her chopsticks onto the table with a sharp clack.

Su Yun'er's heart skipped a beat.

"I had no idea that the monthly allowance of a Marquis's legitimate daughter had become so destitute that she can't even afford a decent meal."

Su Yaoyao stood up. She was taller than Su Yun'er, and as she looked down at her now, she emitted an invisible oppressive aura. "Chuntao."

"This servant is here!"

"Go tell the kitchen." Su Yaoyao said each word clearly, "Go to my mother's shops and have them prepare a few courses of medicinal diet for me. Don't be afraid to spend money, sea cucumbers, abalone, shark's fin, whatever is good, use it! Starting today, my three meals will be prepared according to medicinal diets!"

Chuntao gave a ringing acknowledgment. "Yes! This servant will go right now!"

"You...!" Su Yun'er was both shocked and angered.

"Elder sister, how can you be so extravagant! The Concubine has a hard time managing the household, you..."

"Managing the household is hard, so she treats the legitimate daughter like a beggar?" Su Yaoyao raised an eyebrow. "Or are you saying my mother's dowry is something I, myself, am no longer worthy to use?"

Su Yun'er looked as though she had been stepped on her tail. In the past, this legitimate elder sister had never dared speak to her like this. "Elder sister, what nonsense are you talking about! Auntie manages the household with absolute fairness..."

"Fairness?" Su Yaoyao smiled, her smile bone-chillingly cold.

"Then this jade bracelet on your wrist has quite a nice luster. And this golden hairpin on your head is newly made, isn't it? Whose... silver did you use to pay for it?"

Su Yun'er instinctively covered the bracelet on her wrist, her expression changing completely.

This bracelet, as well as the hairpin, were indeed added to her by the Concubine just a few days ago, and both came from... Su Yaoyao's mother's lavish dowry shops!

"I... I..."

"Younger sister doesn't need to explain." Su Yaoyao waved her hand and sat back down, her posture lazy.

"After all, she is your birth mother. I'm just curious, if Father finds out that not only my mother's dowry, but even his official salary has been 'affectionately' sent to your uncle's gambling table, what would he think?"

Struck as if by lightning, Su Yun'er jerked her head up, staring at Su Yaoyao in terror.

She... how did she know about her uncle gambling?! The Concubine had kept that tightly under wraps!

Su Yaoyao looked at her instantly pale face and sneered inwardly.

The original owner's memories didn't contain this, but Su Yaoyao, having swum in the secular circles of her past life, was best at reading expressions, fishing for words, and analyzing clues.

Liu Concubine was merely a concubine; where did she get the money to maintain a luxurious lifestyle while also subsidizing her maiden family? It wasn't hard to guess.

"Elder sister... elder sister is talking nonsense. My uncle, he..." Su Yun'er still tried to argue.

"Whether I am talking nonsense, younger sister knows best." Su Yaoyao stopped looking at her, turning back to sit before the dressing table, playing with the plain silver hairpin.

"Right, go back and tell the Concubine that I have come of age. The dowry list left by my mother, as well as the storehouse keys, trouble her to send them over in the next couple of days. If the Concubine finds it troublesome..."

She paused, watching Su Yun'er's instantly drained face, and said leisurely,

"I don't mind inviting my maternal grandfather to personally help me manage it. Oh, by the way, I remember the Concubine... was originally a maid sent over as a dowry attendant by Grandmother, wasn't she!"

Su Yun'er's brain gave a loud buzz. "You!"

"What about me? Is there something wrong with my mother's dowry?"

Su Yun'er bit her lip and forced out, "N-no such thing... T-then younger sister won't disturb elder sister any longer."

She turned to leave, but stopped, looking back to say, "Elder sister, three days from now at the palace banquet... His Royal Highness the Crown Prince will also be there. Elder sister's health... it's best to restrain yourself a bit, lest you offend a noble person."

With that, she hurried away.

Su Yaoyao watched her retreating back, the corners of her lips curling upward.

Offend a noble person?

What she feared was not offending them enough.

Watching the Second Prince's concubine-born sister virtually fleeing in a panic, Chuntao burst out laughing, feeling that the pent-up grievance of many years had finally been vented just a little bit.

"Miss, you were amazing!" Her eyes sparkled.

Su Yaoyao showed no trace of smugness, saying indifferently:

"We've barely scratched the surface. These two mother and daughter... heaven knows what else they have waiting for me..."

She glanced at the ginseng soup brought by Su Yun'er.

"The ginseng is subpar, but whatever else they dumped into it was heavy-handed. Take it and pour it out."

No wonder the original owner was listless all day long, aside from not being fed enough, she was also being fed these nasty things...

As for the original owner's mother...

What a coincidence, the heir to a traditional Chinese medicine family; she, Su Yaoyao, had also pursued that in her past life...

The exchange... was also quite in-depth.

chapters.title: The Marquis's Eldest Son
chapters.content:
"Mother! That good-for-nothing, she, she's gone mad!"

Flurried, Su Yun'er ran all the way to Madame Liu's courtyard. The moment she crossed the threshold, her tears began to fall in a flurry.

Madame Liu was currently facing the mirror, tending to her well-preserved face.

"What are you panicking about? Is the sky falling?"

"Mother! It's that bitch Su Yaoyao! She; she really has changed!"

Su Yun'er threw herself onto her mother's lap. "She knows about Uncle's gambling debts! She; she even said she wants to take back her mother's dowry!"

"Did she really say that?" Madame Liu's voice turned chillingly cold.

"It's the absolute truth!" Su Yun'er recounted what had happened in Su Yaoyao's courtyard earlier today, heavily adding her own embellishments.

Madame Liu's expression sank by degrees. She never expected that the eldest legitimate daughter, whom she had manipulated for over a decade and who had been as cowardly as dough, would actually dare to resist! And her very first strike had seized her by the throat!

Su Yun'er clutched her wrist, her heart aching as she touched a jade bracelet of the finest water. Her tears fell even faster. "Will she really go tell Father? And what about her maternal grandfather's family... If they really step in..."

"The Grand Tutor's Estate?" Madame Liu sneered. "Trying to scare me by pulling out the Grand Tutor's Estate?"

She stroked her daughter's delicate and charming face.

"Back then, I was able to make her mother 'fall ill and die,' and make her good older brother 'voluntarily' petition to be posted far away to the borderlands, unable to return for all these years. Grand Tutor Jiang? That old thing retired ages ago... Just a little girl who's barely turned fifteen, and she wants to stir up waves?"

Su Yun'er looked up, her eyes swimming with tears. "But right now... she seems different. Every sentence she speaks carries a thorn. And besides, she took off her chest binder; that figure..."

"Figure?" A heavy wave of jealousy and hatred flashed across the depths of Madame Liu's eyes.

Back then, that woman had stolen the Marquis's heart entirely simply by virtue of her ice-white skin, jade bones, and alluring figure, crushing Madame Liu, who was merely a maid accompanying the bride, leaving her with no chance whatsoever.

If not for the fact that she had resorted to a few methods back then...

Yet now, that woman's daughter, despite all her relentless torment and grinding, had still grown into that devastatingly alluring appearance!

She released her daughter's face, her gaze sharpening. "Yun'er, remember this: as long as you can attach yourself to the Second Prince and get your younger brother made the heir, this Marquis's Estate will be ours in the future! As for Su Yaoyao... what kind of thing is she?"

"But... she still holds the title of the legitimate eldest daughter, and her betrothal to the Second Prince was personally bestowed by His Majesty..." Su Yun'er was still uneasy.

"A betrothal?" Madame Liu sneered. "My silly daughter, don't you see it yet? The Second Prince's eyes right now hold only you. As long as you perform well at the palace banquet and make him thoroughly disgusted with Su Yaoyao, this betrothal might not be unshakeable."

She paused, a calculating glint flashing in her eyes. "And... three days from now at the palace banquet, the Crown Prince will be there too."

Su Yun'er was perplexed. "The Crown Prince? That one who practices Buddhism? What does that have to do with us?"

"Are you foolish?" Madame Liu poked her daughter's forehead. "The Crown Prince practices Buddhism, has a pure heart, and has few desires; he detests frivolous, flirtatious, and unruly women the most. Doesn't Su Yaoyao want to show off? We'll just give her a little help."

Su Yun'er drew in a sharp breath. "B-but that's the Crown Prince... And, and the Empress is also that bitch's own maternal aunt... What if, what if punishment comes down..."

"Punishment?" Madame Liu scoffed. "The Second Prince's birth mother, Noble Consort Chen, is currently at the height of her favor. The Empress? Nobody even knows if her sickly biological son can be raised to adulthood, and although her adopted son is the Crown Prince, he's a useless Buddha. What is she going to use to contend with the Noble Consort?"

She stood up, walked over to the window, and looked out at the opulent pavilions and towers of the Marquis's Estate.

"Your father has wavered back and forth all these years, neither daring to offend the scholarly, upright faction of the Grand Tutor behind the Empress, nor willing to let go of the actual power and benefits given by the Noble Consort. The two of us must fight for ourselves! Once it succeeds, the position of the Second Prince's Consort, and even a higher position in the future... Yun'er, don't you want to thoroughly trample that good-for-nothing beneath your feet and ensure she never rises again?"

Su Yun'er listened, her heart growing hot, yet tinged with a faint, lingering fear.

To scheme against the head of the Empress...

Yet turning to think of her mother's words, thinking of the glory of being the Second Prince's Consort, and thinking of being able to trample Su Yaoyao beneath her feet in the future, that shred of fear was replaced by excitement.

"Daughter understands!"

---

On the other side, Su Yaoyao was soaking in a wooden tub strewn with rose petals.

The warm water wrapped around her skin, and she let out a soft sigh of comfort.

Beneath the surface of the water, her ice-white skin, jade bones, and breathtaking curves were on full display.

Even when she cupped the water and brushed it over herself, she couldn't help but marvel once more at the sheer, God-given endowment of this body.

She scooped up a palmful of ointment mixed with milk and pearl powder, rubbing it meticulously onto her skin.

The foundation of the original owner's skin was simply too good; with just a little nourishment, it revealed an otherworldly, jade-like luster.

Chuntao flushed red as she cautiously helped her ladle water over her shoulders. Looking at the faint bruises left on her young miss's body by the chest binder, she furrowed her brows in deep heartache. "Miss, you've suffered..."

"It's all in the past." Su Yaoyao closed her eyes, feeling the exquisite pleasure of her pores expanding. "From now on, the only thing happening will be me making others suffer."

Suddenly remembering something, she opened her eyes. "Older brother... is there any news from the borderlands?"

Fragments of the original owner's memories surged in her mind, the vague figure of a gentle, warm youth who was her older brother by five years, Su Qingrun.

He would pick flowers for her, teach her how to read characters, and hold her gently while humming the lullabies their mother used to sing when she was alive...

Chuntao's hand, which was ladling the water, paused for a moment, and her voice grew soft and low.

"The eldest young master... last Mid-Autumn Festival, he did manage to have someone send back a box of borderland milk pastries, saying it was for the Miss to taste something fresh. But the things... were intercepted by Madame Liu, who said that crude items from the borderlands were unworthy of entering the Miss's mouth. Afterwards, afterwards there was never any news again..."

In her memories, he had repeatedly stood up for his younger sister, only to be scolded by his father for "disrespecting the concubine mother."

And later on... war broke out at the borderlands, and he actually "actively" volunteered to go. Once he left, it was for several years.

"Actively volunteered..." Su Yaoyao sneered.

An aristocratic heir, the successor to the Marquis's Estate, turning his back on a bright and prosperous future in the capital just to go seek military merits in the bitter, frozen borderlands?

Su Yaoyao's gaze grew progressively colder.

Madame Liu had not only harmed the original owner's mother, but had also engineered a way to ship off her older brother.

An eldest legitimate son who hadn't returned from the borderlands in years, alongside a legitimate daughter who had been raised to be useless... Wasn't this Marquis's Estate completely reduced to the pocket-sized possession of her and her son?

"Brother..." Su Yaoyao whispered these two words, an unfamiliar sourness welling up in her heart; that was the lingering attachment and longing of the original owner.

She raised a hand to stroke her chest, silently vowing:

Rest assured, your brother; I will definitely find a way to bring him back!

Just as she was thinking this, the voice of another little maid rang out from the outer room: "Miss! Someone from the Grand Tutor's Estate is here!"

Su Yaoyao opened her eyes, a flash of expected brilliance crossing her pupils. "Please invite them to wait in the flower parlor; I will be there shortly."

"The Grand Tutor's Estate..." That was her true backing, the blood-connected foundation left to her by her mother.

And her older brother... was another unbroken spine for her in the quagmire of this Marquis's Estate.

Madame Liu thought she could rest easy just by getting rid of her brother?

In her dreams.

Su Yaoyao picked up a comb, slowly smoothing out her half-damp long hair. The person in the mirror looked back with clear and resolute eyes.

She would not only take back her mother's dowry and deal with Madame Liu and her daughter, but she would also welcome her older brother back with all due dignity.

Whosever position the heirship of this Yongning Marquis's Estate was meant to be, it would stay.

"Let's go." She stood up, her moon-white night robe loosely tied, her dark hair cascading down, yet carrying an undeniable aura of grace. "Don't keep the people from the Grand Tutor's Estate waiting."

Su Yaoyao curled the corners of her lips.

Truly worthy of being an aristocratic noble family, swift and decisive. They were completely different from upstart parvenues like the Marquis's Estate.

And they came at just the right time. Madame Liu and her daughter would never sit still and wait for death, and right now, she was lacking trustworthy people.

chapters.title: Begging Me to Take It
chapters.content:
When she arrived at the flower parlor, four people were already standing there in solemn posture.

At the head was a matron of around forty-some years old, with an upright and stern countenance, though her eyes were clear and sharp.

Behind her stood three maids with rigid postures and steady breathing, at a glance clearly having undergone rigorous training.

Seeing Su Yaoyao enter, a flash of swift emotion and heartache crossed the matron's eyes before she bowed properly.

"This old servant, Madam Lin, pays respects to the Eldest Miss. Entrusted by the Old Madame and the Madame, I have come to serve the Eldest Miss."

"This servant, Chengzhe / Guyu / Bailu, pays respects to the Miss."

Su Yaoyao stepped forward and personally helped the matron up. "Matron, please rise quickly. Is Grandmother's health well?"

Seeing her act with such poise and composure, a trace of surprise and relief flashed across Madam Lin's eyes.

Before coming, the Grand Dowager had given repeated instructions, saying the Eldest Miss had been raised to be timid, fearing she would suffer.

Yet the person before her... with clear eyes and a calm demeanor, where was there a single trace of timidity?

"The Old Madame is well, she merely misses the Miss day and night. Upon receiving the Miss's letter and hearing Senior Servant Chuntao describe the situation in the estate, the Old Madame was both furious and heartbroken, and immediately had this old servant bring people over."

She paused, her tone growing slightly heavier. "The Old Madame had this old servant bring a message: The Miss should have done this long ago. The Grand Tutor's Estate will forever be the Miss's backing. What is rightfully yours, not a single fraction can be given up!"

These words were spoken with genuine sincerity. A warmth bloomed in Su Yaoyao's chest. The original owner's maternal family truly cherished her.

"Thank you for your trouble, Matron. Now that I have woken up, I will no longer allow anyone to bully me again."

Madam Lin was immensely gratified and said sternly, "These three girls were specially chosen by the Old Madame for the Eldest Miss. Chengzhe and Guyu possess a foundational understanding of martial arts, while Bailu is meticulous and understands some medical principles; ordinary, underhanded methods cannot slip past her. Only with them guarding your side can the Old Madame feel at ease."

She added, "When I was young, I stayed by the Old Madame's side, managed matters, took charge of households, and gained some experience. If the Eldest Miss has any errands to run, this old servant will not hesitate even unto death."

This was sending all their capable hands over. Su Yaoyao felt moved, knowing this was the Grand Tutor's Estate making their stance explicitly clear: she had someone supporting her!

Su Yaoyao nodded. "Since Matron has arrived, there are indeed a few matters right now where I require your help."

"Please give your instructions, Miss."

Su Yaoyao sat down, resting her head slightly in a troubled manner.

"Yaoyao's constitution is like my mother's, with a weak stomach and spleen, some things simply cannot be eaten... My daily meals will still require Matron to keep a close eye on them." As she spoke, she gently tapped the tabletop.

A chill struck Madam Lin's heart as she understood instantly!

"This servant understands!" She had already known this Marquis's Estate was full of filth, but she never imagined they had been harboring wolves all these years!

Su Yaoyao looked at Madam Lin's expression with satisfaction; as expected of someone from a great household, she caught on with a single hint. Moving forward, this would not only guarantee her own safety, but also allow her to leverage their strength to investigate the truth behind her mother's death.

Though the Grand Tutor had retired, both her uncle and her cousin served in the Dali Temple!

"Also, Madame Liu has been 'safekeeping' my mother's dowry for quite some time now."

Madam Lin's eyes turned sharp. "Does the Miss mean..."

"There's no rush." Su Yaoyao smiled.

"My father... values face above all else, but he is also... somewhat indecisive. If we make the concubine hand it over at this moment, it would at most just carve off a bit of flesh."

She toyed with her teacup.

"What I want is for her to personally hand my mother's belongings back to me, with interest, in full!"

A masterfully confident smile hooked the corners of Su Yaoyao's lips.

"And moreover, she'll have to beg me to take it."

In her past life, the financial bros who used to brag around her didn't hold back on flaunting all sorts of scamming schemes over wine tables. Hearing so much of it, she had managed to figure out a trick or two herself.

No matter how vicious Madame Liu was, she was merely an inner-courtyard woman; what could she possibly know about a "pig-butchering scam"?

She beckoned, and Madam Lin leaned in close.

The matron first furrowed her brows, but instantly her eyes grew brighter and brighter, until finally, a hint of a smile appeared. "The Miss has thought this through comprehensively. This old servant knows what to do."

Su Yaoyao picked up her teacup, took a sip, and softened her tone. "Matron, does Grandmother have any other instructions?"

Madam Lin looked at her with a complex expression and lowered her voice.

"The Old Madame said... you surely understand the Empress's intentions, Miss. It's just that... His Royal Highness the Crown Prince is deep and unfathomable, and dislikes being manipulated by arrangements. The Miss must... exercise extreme caution."

Su Yaoyao smiled slightly.

Caution?

Of course she would exercise caution.

However, caution did not mean failing to press the attack.

"Matron, rest assured," she set down her teacup, light swirling in the depths of her eyes, "in this palace banquet, who arranges whom remains to be seen."

---

The Eastern Palace, Study.

Sandalwood curled in the air. Xiao Chenyuan sat behind his desk, holding a volume of Buddhist scriptures, yet he hadn't turned a single page in quite some time.

His trusted imperial guard, Lingfeng, stood respectfully below. After reporting a few routine court matters, he hesitated and said, "Your Highness, over at the Yongning Marquis's Estate... there seem to be some movements."

Xiao Chenyuan raised his eyes, his gaze calm. "Speak."

The hidden guard kept his head lowered. "The Eldest Miss of the Su family fell ill, and upon waking... her temperament seems to have changed. People from the Grand Tutor Shen's estate entered the Marquis's Estate and went straight to the Eldest Miss's courtyard. Additionally, over at Madame Liu's side, she appears to be secretly contacting a managing eunuch in Noble Consort Chen's palace."

Xiao Chenyuan sat behind the desk, turning a new string of purple sandalwood prayer beads between his fingers.

When he heard the words "Eldest Miss Su," the fingers turning the prayer beads paused imperceptibly.

"And what else?"

"Furthermore, His Highness the Second Prince... has recently been interacting very closely with the Second Miss of the Su family. Acting in this manner, isn't he afraid of offending the Grand Tutor's Estate?"

Xiao Chenyuan raised his eyes.

On the desk lay a newly delivered letter.

It came from the Grand Tutor's Estate.

In the letter, Xiao Chenyuan's mentor, Grand Tutor Shen, rarely used a personal tone. He mentioned that his granddaughter "seems to have had an awakening recently," but because her "temperament is straightforward, if her words or actions at the palace banquet are improper, I hope Your Highness will look to the fact that she lost her mother at a young age and show her some leniency."

Lost her mother at a young age...

Xiao Chenyuan's mind suddenly flashed to a scene from many years ago.

Back then he was only ten years old, following the Grand Tutor to the Marquis's Estate. In the back courtyard garden, there had been a little girl carved out of pink jade, around five or six years old, clumsily trying to pluck a begonia fruit from a branch, standing on tiptoe yet unable to reach it.

He happened to be passing by and casually picked one for her.

The little girl had looked at him with bright, sparkling eyes and said in a sweet, childish voice, "Thank you, Big Brother Crown Prince!"

Later on, the Grand Tutor told him that was his granddaughter, who had just lost her mother.

And after that... he occasionally saw her at palace banquets, always with her head lowered and shoulders hunched, following behind his second brother like a flower that withered before it even bloomed.

He had asked the Grand Tutor about it, but the Grand Tutor merely sighed and said that inner-courtyard matters were inconvenient to meddle in.

To think...

"Your Highness," a eunuch's cautious voice interrupted his thoughts, "Grand Tutor Shen's letter..."

Xiao Chenyuan lowered his eyelashes, his gaze falling upon the final line of the letter...

"Yaoyao has a simple temperament. If someone intentionally misguides her, she might stray from the right path. Hoping Your Highness will remember our bond as master and disciple, and when necessary... pull her along."

He remained silent for a long time before slowly folding the letter.

"Tell the Grand Tutor,"

he spoke, his voice devoid of any emotion, "this orphan knows."

After the eunuch withdrew, Xiao Chenyuan stood up and walked over to the window.

A few pear trees were planted in the courtyard of the Eastern Palace, and right in the middle of their blooming season, snow-white petals drifted down with the wind.

The prayer beads spun across his fingertips.

chapters.title: A Brilliant Entrance
chapters.content:
On the day of the imperial banquet, the festive lanterns were just being lit.

The Imperial Garden was already aflutter with fragrant garments and buzzing with noise.

Noble young ladies of various households gathered in groups of twos and threes, whispering and laughing, yet their gazes constantly, if faintly, drifted toward the entrance...

After all, today was the Crown Prince’s first banquet hosted since his return to the capital.

Today, Su Yun'er had purposely dressed in a pale pink flowing gauze skirt. She leaned against several friendly noble ladies like a delicate willow branch in the wind, though she could not conceal the triumph in the corners of her eyes and brows.

"…Sisters, please stop making fun of me. His Second Highness is merely showing me some extra consideration for my father's sake."

Li Yan, the legitimate daughter of the Minister of Works, covered her smile with a round fan:

"Oh, still acting shy, are we? Who doesn't know that for your sake, the Second Prince didn't even give the legitimate eldest sister a pleasant look at her coming-of-age ceremony? If you ask me, Yun'er, your gentleness and understanding are far better than certain people who hold the title of legitimate daughter yet lack all sense of propriety."

Several young misses nearby chimed in, their words implicitly stepping on Su Yaoyao while praising Su Yun'er.

Su Yun'er enjoyed this inwardly, but outwardly she feigned panic: "Sisters, please don't say such things… The eldest sister, she; she just has a rather straightforward temperament, not on purpose. The other day when I went to visit her, she even reprimanded me for dressing too brightly and losing the Grand Tutor's estate's dignity."

Miss Wang, daughter of the Minister of War, raised an eyebrow: "With that face of hers, she still has the nerve to lecture others?"

"Exactly!" Li Yan sneered. "The last time I saw her, she was sallow and thin, wearing drab gray clothes like some nun who ran away from a temple!"

Miss Wang scoffed: "If you ask me, Su Yaoyao is simply out of her mind. Second Highness clearly fancies someone sensible and well-read like Sister Yun'er, yet she insists on throwing herself at him. Isn't she just asking to be humiliated?"

Su Yun'er feigned anger: "You must not speak of my sister like that. She is the legitimate daughter and the eldest sister; reprimanding me is only right..."

Before her voice faded, an arrogant male voice cut in:

"She actually dared to reprimand you?!"

Everyone looked up to see Xiao Qiming wearing a treasure-blue brocade robe, his hair bound by a jade crown, his face full of anger.

"Su Yaoyao bullied you again?"

"Sister is the legitimate daughter... reprimanding me is only right." Su Yun'er lowered her eyelids, looking deeply wronged. "It's just... Sister said I don't know the rules and shouldn't... shouldn't get too close to Your Highness."

"Such nerve!"

Xiao Qiming was predictably provoked.

"Does she have any self-awareness regarding her own virtues?! A fool who tightens her chest and starves herself all day long dares to lecture you?!"

Seeing Su Yun'er's pear blossoms drenched in rain, his heart softened and he took her hand.

"Rest assured, today I will definitely make her kneel and kowtow to apologize to you!"

Su Yun'er felt triumphant inside, but outwardly she looked even more pitiful: "Your Highness, please don't say that... After all, Sister, Sister is betrothed to you... It doesn't matter if Yun'er suffers a little grievance..."

The more "sensible" she acted, the more Xiao Qiming pitied her, and the more he loathed Su Yaoyao.

"Betwrothment?" Xiao Qiming pulled Su Yun'er's shoulder into his embrace.

"Yun'er, I only have eyes for you! Once I marry that ugly creature into the manor, I will immediately elevate you to the status of co-wife. I will never wrong you!"

He said this as a matter of course, as if it were a settled deal.

As soon as these words came out, the surroundings quieted down by several degrees.

A co-wife? Wouldn't that mean standing on equal footing with the legitimate daughter? The Second Prince was... not leaving Su Yaoyao an ounce of face.

However, Su Yun'er’s heart sank.

A co-wife?

She refused to share a husband with Su Yaoyao! What she wanted was the position of Second Prince's Consort, and to make Su Yaoyao completely vanish!

"Your Highness..." She raised her tearful eyes. "Don't you hate Sister the most? Why must you still marry her?"

Xiao Qiming frowned, looking somewhat impatient:

"It's all because of Imperial Concubine Mother! Saying the Grand Tutor's estate has disciples and followers all over the court, and insisting I marry her! Yun'er, you have no idea how sick I feel just looking at her sallow face! And that figure, it's simply shameless! Unlike you, naturally unadorned, a delicate willow in the wind; now that is a true beauty!"

He spoke through gritted teeth, as if he had suffered the greatest grievance in the world.

Su Yun'er dug her fingernails into her palms, but still had to maintain an understanding smile on her face.

Family background... always family background!

Just because her own birth mother was a maidservant?

No, she would never resign herself to fate!

She took a deep breath and said softly: "Your Highness, do not be angry. Today is the imperial banquet; we should be happy."

Yet in her heart, she had already sliced Su Yaoyao into a thousand pieces.

Just wait, Su Yaoyao. After today, I will ruin your reputation and make the Second Prince retch just at the sight of you!

At that moment, a faint commotion suddenly came from the entrance.

It seemed someone was heading this way.

First came the sound of maidservants sucking in cold breath, followed by the crisp crash of a cup accidentally hitting the ground,

And then... the increasingly obvious, repressed gasps of astonishment.

Xiao Qiming impatiently frowned: "What's going on? All this noise..."

His voice cut off abruptly.

Everyone's gazes involuntarily cast toward the entrance of the Imperial Garden.

In the intertwined light of moonlight and palace lanterns, a slender figure slowly walked over.

That person wore a red ruqun, the hem embroidered with sparse, scattered magnolias using silver thread. As she walked, shimmering light drifted slightly, as if she were stepping on the moon.

The most fatal part was her figure.

Her waist was so slender it seemed it could be spanned by a single grip, loosely tied with a matching woven brocade belt, making her willow-like waist appear even more pronounced.

And looking upward... was a breathtakingly full curve. The neckline was cut to absolute perfection, revealing a section of snow-white neck without being overly exposed, possessing instead a lazy, alluring charm.

She did not wear an elaborate hair bun; her dark hair was only half-coiled, secured with a mutton-fat white jade hairpin, while the rest cascaded like a waterfall down to her waist.

She wore a light dusting of powder on her face, her lips naturally red without paint, and her brows dark without being drawn.

Her skin glowed translucently under the palace lanterns, like fine, warm jade.

Most captivating were her eyes, clear and bright, the outer corners slightly upturned, shifting with radiant light in every glance, carrying a careless yet soul-stealing charm.

She walked thusly, steps composed and waist swaying gently, every movement feeling as though it were treading upon the tips of people's hearts.

Wherever she passed, the autumn scenery of the entire garden seemed to lose its color.

The entire waterside pavilion fell into dead silence.

Everyone was dumbfounded.

This; this is...

"Su Yaoyao, the legitimate daughter of the Marquis of Yongning, arriving..."

The eunuch's shrill announcement rang out like a stone dropped into a calm lake.

"Whoosh..."

After a brief silence came an even greater uproar.

"That's... Su Yaoyao?!"

"My god, that figure... that face..."

"Didn't they say she was sallow, thin, and haggard? This, this..."

Countless gazes nailed themselves to that figure, filled with shock, amazement, jealousy, and utter disbelief.

The handkerchief in Su Yun'er's hand was practically shredded.

She widened her eyes, staring fixedly at the woman walking closer step by step, her nails digging deeply into her palms.

Impossible... This is impossible!

That good-for-nothing... that good-for-nothing she had trampled beneath her feet for over a decade... how could she...

As for Xiao Qiming, he was completely frozen.

chapters.title: Playing the Green Tea? That’s My Specialty
chapters.content:
He stared at the figure not far away, his eyes locked in a fixed gaze.

The fluttering sleeves of her dress made her ice-like skin and jade-like bones appear even more translucent.

Her waist was so thin a single hand could span it, and the curve of her chest... his Adam's apple involuntarily rolled.

And that face overflowing with charm...

Th-this was Su Yaoyao?!

That fiancée he had loathed for years?

Since when... did she grow to look like this?

"Your Highness?" Su Yun'er noticed his lapse and, her internal alarm bells ringing wildly, called out to him softly.

Xiao Qiming acted as if he hadn't heard, his eyes still glued to Su Yaoyao.

Su Yaoyao acted completely oblivious to the gazes filling the courtyard, walking with a composed gait and a faint, proper smile curving her lips.

"Your Highness, Sister."

She nodded slightly, her voice clear and melodious, carrying a trace of a lazy, husky edge. "What a coincidence."

Xiao Qiming abruptly pulled his hand back as if burned, his Adam's apple bobbing. He opened his mouth, but not a single word came out.

The woman before him was so unfamiliar it startled him, yet... so breathtaking he couldn't tear his eyes away.

Seeing the Second Prince like this, the jealousy and hatred in Su Yun'er's heart grew even fiercer.

"Sister's dress... must be newly made, right? The color is indeed bright, but this style..."

She feigned hesitation. "Isn't it... a bit too revealing of your figure? Today's imperial banquet is attended by the Crown Prince as well. Sister should still... strive to be more dignified."

These words sounded like praise on the surface while being derogatory underneath, directly pointing out that Su Yaoyao's attire was inappropriate and carried the suspicion of frivolity.

Sure enough, upon hearing this, several older matrons cast a scrutinizing gaze toward Su Yaoyao.

Before Su Yaoyao could speak, a young lord in blue nearby couldn't help but chime in: "Second Miss Su speaks wrongly. Eldest Miss Su's appearance is outstanding, and her attire is completely appropriate. She looks lovely!"

Another person echoed: "Indeed. In my view, Eldest Miss Su's attire is refined and otherworldly, far superior to those dripping in gold and silver."

These words were pointed. The complexions of several noble young ladies who had just mocked Su Yaoyao instantly turned ugly.

Su Yaoyao smiled slightly at the young men, causing them to blush to the tips of their ears.

Looking at her charming and beaming smile, a surge of vicious fire flared up in Su Qiming, and he sneered, "Dressed up all flashy, who are you trying to show off to? Shameless!"

Su Yaoyao turned her gaze to him, a flash of the faintest mockery crossing the depths of her eyes, too fast for anyone to catch.

Instantly, a hazy layer of moisture welled up in those beautiful eyes.

Then, she lowered her head slightly, her voice trembling:

"Second Prince... you really didn't need to humiliate me like this. Yaoyao... understands in her heart..."

She raised her eyes, tears welling up on the verge of falling, yet her gaze remained crystal clear, carrying a shattered resilience:

"His Highness and Younger Sister are a match made in heaven; Yaoyao has seen it with her own eyes."

Su Yaoyao's voice was soft and gentle, yet it carried clearly all around.

"Although Yaoyao is betrothed to Your Highness, I have no wish to play the villain who seizes what others love and obstructs a good match..."

At this point, she wore the expression of someone enduring deep grievances yet forcing herself to stay strong.

"Since this betrothal... was bestowed by His Majesty, humble as I am, I dare not comment. But if Your Highness and Younger Sister truly love one another..."

She bit her lip, her full lips turning a vivid shade of red under the bite, causing several young lords' hearts to skip a beat.

"Rest assured, Your Highness. If Your Highness truly does not wish for this marriage, even if Yaoyao has to go before Imperial Aunt to kneel for three days and nights, kowtowing and begging, I will surely... surely beg Imperial Aunt to grant Your Highness and Younger Sister your wish, so that lovers may finally become spouses."

With that, a single tear dropped at the exact right moment, rolling down her glowing white cheek.

A beauty in tears, enough to melt anyone's heart.

Silence.

Deathly silence.

Look at Su Yaoyao, who was on the verge of weeping yet forced back her sorrow, wishing only to "fulfill" others.

Then look at the aggressive Second Prince, who protected his concubine-born sister-in-law while showing zero respect for his legitimate fiancée.

And then look at Su Yun'er hiding behind the Second Prince, seemingly fragile yet actually baiting the Second Prince into publicly degrading the legitimate eldest sister.

The difference was stark!

Already, several soft-hearted young misses had their eyes turning red, pressing handkerchiefs to the corners of their eyes.

"Eldest Miss Su... is simply too pitiful."

"Indeed, clearly she's the one who has been wronged..."

"She's the proper, legitimate fiancée, yet she has to watch her fiancé act all cozy with someone else..."

"And she's even this magnanimous, saying she wants to fulfill their wishes..."

"As for Second Miss Su... usually she looks so fragile, how could she..."

"The Second Prince goes too far!"

Xiao Qiming hung his jaw, staring at Su Yaoyao's tear-blurred yet stunningly beautiful face, listening to the faint condemnation around him, his mind in complete chaos.

Before, he used to find Su Yaoyao's crying annoying, but now...

Why did that tear make his heart race with panic?

And what she said about calling off the marriage... he suddenly realized that he seemed... not nearly as pleased by the idea as he had imagined?

Besides, she loved him this much, willing to kneel and beg just to fulfill his wishes...

Doesn't this... doesn't this just prove she had feelings for him in her heart?

He opened his mouth, wanting to say, "Good thing you know your place," but the words turned into: "Y-you know that's good! However... the betrothal was bestowed by Imperial Father, it's not something that can be broken off just like that..."

Su Yun'er was even more shocked and furious.

His Highness's tone... why did it sound like he was reluctant to let go?!

And this bitch! When did she learn this trick of retreating to advance, playing the pitiful card to win sympathy?!

She was even better at acting than she was!

Seeing the situation turning against her, she hurriedly squeezed out tears: "Sister, please don't say that... Yun'er never thought of competing with Sister. As long as I can serve by His Highness's side, Yun'er is utterly content..."

As she spoke, she made to kneel, only to be yanked up by Xiao Qiming.

"Yun'er, what are you doing!" Xiao Qiming pulled her into his arms with a distressed expression, then looked back at Su Yaoyao with a complicated gaze.

Inwardly, Su Yaoyao sneered.

Oh, starting a contest on who can cry more pathetically now?

She gently dabbed the corners of her eyes with a handkerchief, her voice growing even softer: "Younger Sister, please stop crying... Rest assured, Sister will keep her word. Only..."

She paused, looking at Xiao Qiming with a hesitant expression: "Only, Yaoyao is worried that if this betrothal is truly called off, and Your Highness marries Younger Sister instead, it might provoke gossip, saying Younger Sister... saying Younger Sister seduced her future brother-in-law while Sister was gravely ill..."

"What nonsense are you spouting!" Xiao Qiming's expression changed.

Su Yaoyao hurriedly shook her head, tears finally rolling down: "Yaoyao didn't mean that! Younger Sister is innocent and kind-hearted, how could she do such a thing? It's just people outside running their mouths... Yaoyao is merely worried about Younger Sister's reputation..."

As she spoke, she covered her face with her handkerchief, her shoulders trembling slightly, crying in a way that drew utter pity.

The gazes the noble ladies cast toward Su Yun'er had already shifted.

Indeed... Second Miss Su was inseparable from the Second Prince all day long, it really wasn't very proper...

Su Yun'er trembled all over with anger, yet she still had to maintain her fragile image, turning green in the face for a moment.

Su Yaoyao increased the pressure, her eyes sweeping back and forth between the two.

She offered a bitter smile, a smile so shattered it broke the heart.

"Yaoyao understands. Rest assured, Your Highness, Yaoyao... will no longer harbor any extravagant hopes."

With that, she curtsied slightly, offered a bow, and turned to walk toward her own seat.

The hem of her skirt brushed across the smooth floor, her hair ornaments swaying lightly, her back slender yet straight.

Leaving behind a garden full of varied gazes and an iron-faced Xiao Qiming.

He stared at that retreating back, a nameless irritation suddenly welling up in his chest.

Su Yun'er leaned into his embrace, feeling his momentary distraction, and her internal alarm bells went crazy.

No... this good-for-nothing, today she was far too abnormal!

She had to execute her plan as soon as possible!

Meanwhile, Su Yaoyao, walking toward her seat, gently wiped away the tear at the corner of her eye from an angle where no one could see, a fleeting, cold smirk curling the corners of her lips.

Dog scum.

Had enough already?

The good show was only just beginning.

She took her seat and looked up toward the main dais...

That seat was still empty.

Crown Prince Xiao Chenyuan had yet to arrive.

Su Yaoyao picked up her wine cup, the amber liquid rippling within.

No rush.

A hunter is always the most patient.

Her true target today... was not that empty-headed Second Prince.

As she thought this, a shrill eunuch's announcement suddenly rang out from the entrance:

"His Royal Highness the Crown Prince arrives..."

The whole garden fell instantly silent.

Su Yaoyao raised her eyes to look.

Amidst the brilliant glow of the palace lanterns, a figure as cold and pristine as snow stepped slowly forward...

chapters.title: The Buddha-like Crown Prince Lowers His Gaze
chapters.content:
In the dead silence of the hall, everyone’s gaze focused on the entrance.

Where the palace lanterns shone the brightest, a figure walked slowly inward.

The man wore a plain white brocade robe, unadorned with jade or crown. In his hand, he twirled a string of agarwood prayer beads, and his dark hair was secured with a simple ebony hairpin.

Yet, dressed in such extreme minimalism, he carried an aura of ethereal nobility that far surpassed the mortal realm.

Su Yaoyao raised her eyes, and her fingers, gripping her wine cup, tightened fiercely.

What, in, the, name, of, heaven, is, this, supreme, specimen!

She had spent so long mingling in the high-stakes world of her past life; what kind of handsome men hadn’t she seen?

Yet this one before her... the absolute ceiling of the cold, abstinence-style aesthetic, radiating a natural aura of sacred holiness, yet blessed with a face that could make a person lose all self-control.

His figure was tall and straight, his features exceedingly refined, with a high bridge of the nose and very pale lips.

And the most peerless part was his eyes; their shape was exceptionally fine, yet his pupils were lighter in shade than ordinary people's, like black jade submerged in a cold pool. When he cast a faint glance at people, devoid of waves or ripples, it possessed an inherent, piercing clarity that saw right through the heart.

The lamplight falling upon him seemed to consciously dim by three parts.

Yet what attracted Su Yaoyao the most was not these striking facial features, but the contradictory yet harmonious aura about him.

Cold. Ascetic. Untouched by the mortal dust.

Like a Buddha carved from white jade, looking down with compassion upon all living beings in the floating world.

Su Yaoyao blinked, and the urge to conquer flared up with a sudden "whoosh."

Interesting.

Far too interesting.

If a man like this could be made to have his cold eyes stained with desire, to have the indifferent corners of his lips curve for her, to have the mirror-calm lake of his heart ripple for her...

Just thinking about it made her heart race.

The higher the difficulty, the greater the challenge, and the more she loved it.

Xiao Chenyuan seemed to sense something, and his gaze swept faintly across the entire hall.

Wherever it passed, the noble daughters lowered their heads, not daring to meet his gaze directly.

The bold ones raised their eyes in secret, only to hastily lower them again the moment they touched those deep-pool eyes.

His gaze finally landed on Su Yaoyao.

It was a very brief glance.

Yet Su Yaoyao sharply caught a trace of an extremely faint... astonishment within that gaze?

Immediately, that gaze shifted away, as though she were no different from anyone else in the crowded garden.

Xiao Chenyuan walked to the seat below the main throne and sat down. Palace attendants immediately stepped forward to serve tea.

He picked up his teacup, his slender fingers like jade, his movements unhurried, the very arc of his fluttering sleeves exuding a sense of Zen.

He did not utter a single word the entire time, yet he had already become the center of the entire hall.

Su Yaoyao withdrew her gaze, the corners of her lips curving slightly.

Very well.

The more difficult a man like this was to tease, the greater the sense of accomplishment.

Just as she was thinking this, a slight commotion suddenly erupted diagonally across from her.

A noble lady dressed in a goose-yellow palace gown, likely instigated by her elders to win a promising future, mustered her courage. Holding a cup of wine, she stood up and walked gracefully toward the Crown Prince's seat.

"This subject's daughter... this subject's daughter toasts Your Highness the Crown Prince."

Yet she "carelessly" slipped, let out a cry of alarm, and fell toward Xiao Chenyuan.

She was dressed lightly today, and her collar was deliberately loosened a bit. This fall would undoubtedly be a fragrant and seductive embrace.

The breath of the entire hall hitched.

Su Yaoyao raised an eyebrow, waiting to watch a good show.

Yet Xiao Chenyuan didn't even lift an eyelid.

Lingfeng, the stern-faced guard at his side, stepped forward with lightning speed, cupped the young lady's shoulder with one hand, and pushed backward...

The force was controlled with extreme precision. The young lady staggered back a few steps and collapsed to the ground, her hair bun even coming undone, yet she hadn't touched even a shred of the Crown Prince's robe.

"In the presence of His Highness, act with restraint." Lingfeng's voice was as cold as ice.

Only then did Xiao Chenyuan turn his head slightly to glance at the pale-faced young lady sitting in a heap on the ground.

That look was so devoid of emotion that it was as if he were looking not at a human being, but at a speck of dust.

"Drag her out."

He spoke, his voice indifferent yet carrying authority, "Disturbing the imperial banquet, confined to quarters for three months."

Two eunuchs immediately stepped forward, covered the mouth of the young lady who still wanted to cry and plead, and briskly dragged her away.

The hall was pin-drop silent.

The noble daughters who had still been harboring restless thoughts all reined in their ambitions at this moment, lowering their heads to stare at the hems of their skirts, not daring to spare even a half-glance toward the Crown Prince.

Su Yun'er took in everything before her, her heart filled with wild joy.

Splendid!

The Crown Prince was truly as the rumors said, keeping women at a distance to an almost harsh degree! Even a beauty who threw herself into his arms was directly dragged away without an ounce of mercy.

As long as Su Yaoyao was made to make a fool of herself before the Crown Prince, leaving an impression of being unrestrained and frivolous, out of disgust, the Crown Prince might even fly into a rage on the spot.

By then, not only would Su Yaoyao's reputation be utterly ruined, but even her aunt, the Empress, would lose face!

Su Yun'er sneered inwardly.

Su Yaoyao, did you think that by changing your skin you could catch the Crown Prince's eye?

In your dreams!

Just wait... there will come a time for you to cry!

She gave a look to the maid standing behind her. The maid understood and quietly retreated.

Meanwhile, Su Yaoyao at her seat gently swirled her wine cup, a trace of playful interest flitting across the depths of her eyes.

This Crown Prince was... even harder to handle than she had imagined.

Yet what could she do?

She seemed to... like him even more now.

Before long, the music gradually rose, and a troupe of dancers in light gauze fluttered in, dancing gracefully in the center of the banquet.

The string and woodwind music was pleasing to the ear, and the dance postures were enchanting. The atmosphere of the banquet became lively once again.

Su Yaoyao appeared to be enjoying the song and dance, but in reality, she was watching all directions and listening to all sides.

She noticed that the maid by Su Yun'er's side was gone.

She also noticed that among the dancers, one possessed an exceptionally slender figure and a particularly dazzling beauty. As she danced, her amorous glances frequently drifted toward the Crown Prince's seat, and her waist twisted with extraordinary softness.

She noticed even more that the dancer's sleeve seemed to conceal something.

Su Yaoyao lowered her gaze, the corners of her lips curling into a playful smirk.

It's coming.

Sure enough, when the tune ended and the dancers bowed to withdraw, that exceptionally dazzling dancer suddenly slipped, let out an "Aiya" cry of alarm,

And as luck would have it, the direction she fell was none other than Su Yaoyao's seat!

The moment she fell, a small pouch of powdered substance suddenly flew out from her sleeve, scattering straight toward Su Yaoyao’s face!

In a flash of lightning, Su Yaoyao’s gaze turned sharp.

If she dodged, that powder would inevitably scatter onto her person.

If this moon-bright flowing brocade dress she wore today were stained with dust, she would undoubtedly look disheveled.

If she didn't dodge...

What kind of thing was inside that powder was anyone's guess.

Su Yun'er, you are truly ruthless.

Su Yaoyao’s thoughts spun rapidly. At the split second before the powder was about to touch her face, she let out a "panicked" low cry, and the wine cup in her hand "accidentally" slipped...

"Clatter!"

The wine cup hit the floor, the sound of shattering crisp.

And taking advantage of the movement to dodge by rising, her wide sleeves flicked, actually brushing away the vast majority of the powder, leaving only a tiny bit stained on her cuff.

At the same time, her foot seemed to catch on something, and her whole body "staggered" as she fell sideways...

The direction she fell was, precisely, toward the Crown Prince’s seat!

Everything happened in a fraction of a second.

The crowd only saw the dancer fall, the powder fly, Su Yaoyao rise in panic, the wine cup shatter, and then her footing become unstable, looking as though she was about to fall to the ground...

And the Crown Prince, Xiao Chenyuan, was seated directly ahead of where she was falling!

If she truly fell, she would inevitably crash into the Crown Prince's arms!

Wild joy flashed in Su Yun'er’s eyes.

It's done!

Yet the next moment, everyone froze.

They saw that at the very instant she was about to fall, Su Yaoyao suddenly reached out and accurately grabbed the edge of the... low table beside the Crown Prince’s seat.

She used the leverage to steady her posture. Though her posture was somewhat disheveled, her hair bun slightly disordered, and her hairpins swaying softly, she ultimately did not truly fall.

Nor did she touch so much as a fraction of the Crown Prince.

After steadying herself, her very first action was not to tidy her appearance, but to turn toward Xiao Chenyuan, curtsy in salute, her voice carrying a perfectly measured panic and guilt:

"This subject's daughter has lost her composure and startled Your Highness. Please forgive this sin, Your Highness."

She kept her head lowered, revealing a stretch of white, graceful the back of her neck.

Because of the previous "panic," her cheeks flushed with a faint rosy tint, her eye rims were also slightly red, and her long eyelashes trembled like the wings of a startled butterfly.

That appearance was both pitiful and strictly observant of propriety.

Xiao Chenyuan raised his eyes and looked at her.

This was the second time tonight he had looked at her properly.

His gaze lingered for a split second on her slightly red eye rims, then landed on that imperceptible speck of powder on her cuff.

Finally, he looked toward the dancer who was still sprawled on the ground with a pale face.

"Lingfeng," he spoke, his voice still calm and waveless, "investigate."
