"Understood!" Lingfeng acknowledged, walking briskly toward the dancer.

At that moment, the eunuch’s loud proclamation suddenly sounded from the entrance:

"Her Majesty the Empress has arrived..."

The entire hall hurriedly stood up to salute.

Su Yaoyao also curtsied along with the crowd, yet as she lowered her head, the corners of her lips curved into a fleeting smile.

Empress Aunt, you have arrived at precisely the right time.

The good show has only just begun.

chapters.title: Aphrodisiac
chapters.content:
The Empress arrived, and the entire hall fell solemn.

She wore a phoenix robe. Though over forty, she was well-preserved, her brows and eyes three parts similar to Su Yaoyao's, save for the added majesty of one who had long resided in a position of supremacy.

"Rise," the Empress said, taking her seat on the main throne, her voice gentle. "Today's banquet is to welcome the Crown Prince; you need not stand on ceremony."

She looked at Xiao Chenyuan, her gaze affectionate: "Yuan'er, you've had a hard journey."

Xiao Chenyuan rose and saluted: "Thank you for your concern, Mother Empress. This son is not tired."

His tone was respectful, yet reeked of distance.

A trace of complexity flashed across the Empress's eyes, quickly concealed, and she smiled: "Everyone sit. Just now outside, it seemed I heard some commotion inside?"

Su Yun'er was secretly overjoyed; she hastily stood up and said softly: "Reporting to Your Majesty, just now... just now it was merely an accident. Older Sister she... she did not intentionally startle the Crown Prince."

These words were spoken with clever artifice. Seeming to absolve Su Yaoyao, they actually cemented her crime of "startling the Crown Prince."

Xiao Qiming watched from the side, unable to help frowning. Though he felt Su Yaoyao was indeed somewhat different tonight, seeing Su Yun'er speak up for her with such grievance while Su Yaoyao merely stood there pretending to be pitiful, that wave of annoyance surged up in his chest again.

He let out a cold snort and spoke up: "Mother Empress, this son also saw it just now. Eldest Miss Su's behavior was indeed improper, and she startled Crown Prince Imperial Elder Brother. However..." He glanced at Su Yaoyao, his tone carrying mockery,

"She has always been like this; not understanding rules is not a matter of just a day or two. I ask that Mother Empress and Imperial Elder Brother please not hold her at fault."

As soon as these words left his mouth, quite a few people secretly drew in a breath.

The Second Prince wasn't leaving his fiancée even an ounce of face!

The Empress’s face darkened slightly, and just as she was about to speak, Su Yaoyao spoke first:

"Reporting to Aunt... Just now, this dancer carelessly fell, and the powder flying from her sleeve nearly scattered onto this subject's daughter's face. In a moment of panic, this subject's daughter accidentally shattered her wine cup, and that was why... why she nearly clashed with His Highness the Crown Prince."

When she spoke, she lowered her head slightly, her posture respectful yet maintaining grace.

A trace of astonishment swept through the Empress's eyes.

This niece of hers... seemed truly different now.

When she saw her in the past, she was always cowering, her voice as small as a mosquito's when she spoke, her gaze dodging, presenting a thoroughly unpresentable appearance. But today...

Her behavior was proper, her responses measured, and what was even rarer was that calm composure emanating from her very bones.

And this appearance...

The Empress's gaze lingered for a moment on Su Yaoyao's exquisitely clear and beautiful face, then glanced at Su Yun'er, whose expression was unsightly not far away, and understood in her heart.

"Yaoyao wasn't frightened, was she? Come quickly to my side and let me have a look."

This was undisguised favoritism.

Su Yaoyao obediently walked to the Empress's side. The Empress took her hand, looked carefully at her complexion, and then glanced at the speck of powder on her cuff, her brows furrowing imperceptibly.

"Such a pity, even this dress is soiled." The Empress patted her hand.

Seeing this, Su Yun'er hastily tugged on Xiao Qiming's sleeve: "Your Highness, do not be angry. Sister she... she also did it unintentionally."

These words pulled Xiao Qiming's wits back. He steadied himself, and when he looked at Su Yaoyao again, that inexplicable irritation in his heart grew even heavier, his tone becoming even more caustic: "Unintentional? I think she deliberately wanted to attract attention! Su Yaoyao, don't think that just by changing your clothes you can..."

"Qiming," the Empress interrupted him in a deep voice, "Yaoyao is your fiancée, mind your words."

Xiao Qiming fell sullenly silent, but glared fiercely at Su Yaoyao.

Lingfeng had already escorted the dancer to the front:

"Reporting to Her Majesty the Empress, this dancer concealed an aphrodisiac in her sleeve and intentionally scattered it toward Eldest Miss Su when she fell just now."

The moment the words "aphrodisiac" were uttered, the entire hall erupted in an uproar!

At an imperial banquet, someone actually used such despicable methods?!

The dancer's face turned as pale as paper, trembling all over:

"Th-this servant did not... this servant was careless..."

"Careless?" Xiao Chenyuan suddenly spoke.

He remained seated, twirling the prayer beads in his hand, his tone flat:

"The inner pouch of your sleeve was exquisitely sewn, and the timing and direction of your fall were both precise. Was that carelessness?"

With every sentence he spoke, the dancer's face turned a shade paler.

Finally, Xiao Chenyuan raised his eyes, his gaze falling upon Su Yaoyao: "Has Eldest Miss Su ever harbored enmity with anyone?"

Su Yaoyao praised him inwardly, what a great Crown Prince, with a single sentence he pointed the spearhead directly at the mastermind behind the scenes.

She timely revealed a bewildered expression:

"This subject's daughter... this subject's daughter is seeing her for the first time today, and has no grievances." She paused, as if recalling something, and said softly,

"It's just that earlier... earlier when the powder was scattered, this subject's daughter dazedly heard this songstress whisper, 'Forgive me, Eldest Miss Su; if you want to blame someone, blame yourself for offending someone you shouldn't have'..."

Her voice was not loud, but it was enough for the tables nearby to hear clearly.

"Clatter..."

Discussions broke out all around.

Who had a grudge against Su Yaoyao? And used such despicable means?

Many people's gazes glanced covertly at Su Yun'er.

Su Yun'er's face turned green, and she hastily stood up: "Sister! You cannot speak nonsense! This dancer has no grievances with you, how could she harm you? You must have misheard!"

"Is that so?" Su Yaoyao raised her tear-filled eyes to look at her: "Younger Sister is so certain... Could it be you know some inside story?"

"I... how would I know!" Su Yun'er panicked, "I only thought... thought that Sister was perhaps overly frightened and experienced hallucinations..."

"Enough," the Empress spoke in a deep voice.

Her gaze swept over Su Yun'er, a trace of displeasure flashing in her eyes, and just as she was about to speak...

"Mother Empress."

Xiao Qiming wore an impatient look: "Such a trivial matter, why make such a fuss?"

He walked to Su Yun'er's side, shielding her behind him, and looked coldly at Su Yaoyao: "Su Yaoyao, you lost your own composure and startled Imperial Elder Brother, yet you're still here biting and framing Yun'er? Yun'er is kind-hearted and spoke so many good words for you; is this how you repay her?"

He spoke with righteous indignation, as if he had seen with his own eyes that it was Su Yaoyao's fault.

Su Yaoyao sneered inwardly, but on the surface she looked even more aggrieved: "Second Prince... This subject's daughter is not framing Younger Sister, this subject's daughter is merely... merely stating the facts..."

"Facts?" Xiao Qiming sneered, "When are you not putting on a pitiful act while actually harboring a vicious mind? Yun'er is pure, which is why she's always bullied by you!"

He turned to the Empress, cupping his hands: "Mother Empress, this son believes this matter was simply an accident. This dancer was careless, and Su Yaoyao is cowardly, stirring up this laughingstock. Yun'er was innocently implicated; I ask Mother Empress to clearly discern the truth!"

This turning of black into white was done with blatant shamelessness.

The noble daughters in the hall looked at each other in dismay, a few even secretly curling their lips, the Second Prince's favoritism was simply too obvious.

Su Yun'er leaned against Xiao Qiming's side, lowering her head to conceal the triumph in the depths of her eyes.

Su Yaoyao looked at this pair of "lovebirds," and suddenly said softly: "Second Prince is right... It is this subject's daughter's fault."

Her eye rims grew even redder, yet she held back her tears: "This subject's daughter should not have... should not have appeared here, causing His Highness and Younger Sister displeasure. This subject's daughter will take her leave..."

With that, she made to bow and withdraw.

"Hold on."

The one who spoke was Xiao Chenyuan.

chapters.title: The Buddhist Disciple Tainted by the Red Dust
chapters.content:
He slowly rose, his gaze sweeping over Xiao Qiming: "Second brother, the matter has not been thoroughly investigated, there is no need to rush to a conclusion."

His tone remained level, yet carried an unquestionable authority.

Xiao Qiming faltered: "Imperial elder brother, I..."

"Lingfeng," Xiao Chengyuan stopped looking at him, "escort this woman down and hand her over to the Inner Court for interrogation."

He paused, then added: "As for the Eldest Miss Su..."

He looked at Su Yaoyao.

Su Yaoyao appropriately lowered her head, the speck of powder on her cuff particularly striking under the palace lantern.

"Being frightened was not her fault; on the contrary, she was nearly framed." Xiao Chengyuan’s tone was faint.

Was this... defending her?

Xiao Qiming’s expression turned ugly: "Imperial elder brother! What are you..."

"Second brother."

Xiao Chengyuan raised his eyes to look at him, his gaze bottomless.

Just two casual words, yet they forced Xiao Qiming to swallow back everything he wanted to say.

Su Yaoyao was startled inwardly, then smiled secretly.

This Crown Prince was, after all, a bit... more interesting than she had imagined.

"Thank you, Your Highness, for your consideration." She curtsied.

Amidst her movements, the hair-pin already dangling precariously from her hair swayed gently, shook loose, and fell with a soft "clink," rolling to the ground.

It stopped precisely at Xiao Chengyuan’s feet.

Su Yaoyao let out an "ah" and was about to bend down to pick it up...

A hand with distinct knuckles picked up the hair-pin a step before her.

Xiao Chengyuan lowered his gaze to the hair-pin in his hand.

He stood up and walked over to Su Yaoyao.

The entire hall fell silent, everyone staring wide-eyed.

The Crown Prince... actually picked up jewelry for a woman personally?!

Xiao Chengyuan handed the hair-pin back to her: "Returning it to its rightful owner."

His voice remained cool and detached, but the act itself was scandalous enough to shock the world.

Su Yaoyao looked up at him, her eyes flashing with just the right amount of panic and gratitude: "Thank, thank you, Your Highness..."

She reached out to take it, her fingertips inadvertently brushing lightly against his palm.

A very light touch, like a feather brushing past.

Xiao Chengyuan’s fingertips curled imperceptibly.

Su Yaoyao took the hair-pin, her lips curving slightly as she lowered her head.

Very good.

A reaction meant a good thing.

Watching this scene, Xiao Qiming felt a wave of inexplicable irritation rise in his chest.

That Su Yaoyao, who always followed behind him and whom he despised... when did she become able to make the Crown Prince pick things up for her personally?

And the look she gave the Crown Prince when she looked up just now...

He suddenly felt that gaze to be glaringly offensive.

"Putting on a show," he snorted coldly, pulling Su Yun'er back to their seats.

Su Yun'er was yanked so hard she staggered, turning back to glare fiercely at Su Yaoyao.

The Empress took everything in, ultimately saying nothing.

The banquet continued, but the atmosphere had already turned subtle.

Su Yaoyao sat quietly in her seat. Many noble daughters secretly sized her up, their eyes holding a few more portions of assessment and probing.

Xiao Qiming stared at her for a while, the irritation in his heart growing increasingly fierce.

Especially when he saw the red mark he had pinched earlier still lingering on her fair wrist, he felt an inexplicable guilt.

He picked up his wine cup and gulped it down, only to hear a few young lords nearby whispering:

"The Eldest Miss Su is truly breathtaking tonight..."

"More than breathtaking, that figure... tsk."

"What a pity, the Second Prince seems..."

"Hush, keep it down..."

Xiao Qiming’s face turned livid as he slammed his wine cup down heavily.

Seeing this, Su Yun'er hurriedly poured him a drink, her voice soft: "Your Highness, do not be angry. Elder sister... she perhaps only wanted to attract your attention."

"Attract attention?" Xiao Qiming sneered, "Does she think I’ll look at her more just because of this? In her dreams!"

Though he said this, his eyes involuntarily drifted toward Su Yaoyao again.

Su Yun'er’s fingertips trembled with anger, her teeth almost biting through in fury.

How could this be?! That powder was clearly sprinkled toward her!

How could she have not the slightest reaction?!

That good-for-nothing... when did she become so cunning?!

And the Crown Prince... why would he help Su Yaoyao?!

As she fumed in resentment, her maid quietly crept over and whispered in a low voice:

"Miss, the dancer's family has already been paid off; she won't dare speak nonsense. But... but over at the Inner Court..."

Su Yun'er took a deep breath: "Have Mother find a way. No matter what, it must not lead back to us!"

She stared at Su Yaoyao diagonally across from her, venomous light flashing in her eyes.

If one scheme fails, execute another.

She refused to believe Su Yaoyao could be this lucky every single time!

How could Su Yun'er know that just now, with a sweep of her wide sleeves, Su Yaoyao had, while appearing panicked, applied self-defense techniques learned in her past life, scattering the majority of the powder away.

The small amount remaining on her cuff also failed to immediately seep into her skin due to the special fabric of the garments.

Yet at this moment, Su Yaoyao felt a faint burning sensation at her cuff.

Her heart tightened.

This incense... was its medicinal effect so overbearing? Just clinging to the fabric caused this kind of reaction?

Su Yaoyao stood up, intending to get some air in the imperial garden.

Su Yun'er walked up holding a wine cup: "Elder sister was frightened just now, and this younger sister couldn't help, feeling deeply guilty. I specifically came to make amends..."

Before she finished speaking, her "foot slipped," and the half-cup of leftover wine she held splashed straight toward Su Yaoyao’s chest!

Su Yaoyao’s pupils sharpened.

This time, she didn't dodge.

"Splash..."

The ice-cold wine liquid splashed entirely across her chest.

Under the moonlight, her drenched dress clung tightly to her body, outlining breathtaking curves.

Where the wine stains soaked in, the fabric became semi-translucent, vaguely revealing the pearlescent skin beneath.

Su Yun'er let out a gasp of shock, quickly pulling out a handkerchief: "Oh! Elder sister, I'm sorry! I didn't mean to... I, I'll help you wipe it..."

She reached out to wipe Su Yaoyao’s chest.

Su Yaoyao took a step back, avoiding her hand.

Watching this scene, triumph flashed in Su Yun'er's eyes.

Su Yaoyao, let's see how you get out of this now!

Stay at the banquet with a wet body? That's a grave offense of disrespect!

Not changing clothes? With anyone seeing you looking like this, your reputation will be utterly ruined!

And over at the changing rooms... she had already arranged a "good show" waiting.

Su Yaoyao lowered her gaze to look at her disheveled dress, then raised her eyes to look at Su Yun'er’s hypocritical expression of concern.

Suddenly, she smiled.

A bright smile, yet chillingly cold at the bottom of her eyes.

"Little sister,"

She spoke softly, her voice exceptionally clear in the night wind:

"This cup of wine... you splashed it with incredible accuracy."

chapters.title: The Person She Was Waiting For... Has Arrived
chapters.content:
The night breeze was slightly cool, sweeping across Su Yaoyao’s drenched dress and bringing a chill.

She lowered her head to look at the wine stains blooming across her chest, patchy and clinging tightly to her skin, looking utterly disheveled.

Su Yun'er was still putting on an act with her handkerchief, her eyes red with anxiety:

"Elder sister, I really didn't mean to... It's all the floor tiles' fault for being so slippery... Hurry and come with me to the side hall to change clothes; I; I have clean ones prepared there!"

She reached out to pull Su Yaoyao, but was nimbly evaded.

"What is little sister rushing for?" Su Yaoyao raised her eyes to look at her, a hint of a smile even tugging at the corners of her lips.

"It's just wine spilled on a dress, a wipe will fix it."

As she spoke, she actually took the handkerchief from Su Yun'er's hand and leisurely began wiping the wine stains on her chest.

Her movements were composed; where was there a shred of panic?

Su Yun'er’s heart skipped a beat.

Something was wrong...

Why was this good-for-nothing so calm? Did she not know that walking around the palace with a wet body was a grave offense of impropriety?

Or could it be...

She wasn't afraid at all?

"Elder sister..." Su Yun'er forced a smile,

"I'm afraid these wine stains won't wipe off easily. Shouldn't we go to the side hall to change? I've already had the maids prepare hot water and clean clothes..."

"Little sister is truly thoughtful." Su Yaoyao stopped her movements, tilting her head to look at her with a trace of amusement flashing in her eyes,

"Even hot water is prepared? How did little sister know... I would definitely wet my clothes?"

Su Yun'er’s expression shifted slightly: "I; I was just preparing for the worst..."

"Is that so?"

Su Yaoyao handed the handkerchief back to her and turned to look at the main seat. "But if I go back now and tell the Empress that little sister 'accidentally' splashed a cup of wine all over me, preventing me from continuing the banquet..."

She paused, turning back to look at Su Yun'er’s instantly pale face: "What would Her Majesty think? Would she think little sister deliberately humiliated her legitimate elder sister to monopolize the Second Prince's attention?"

"You!" Su Yun'er almost crushed her teeth.

She took a deep breath, suppressing the anger in her chest, and her voice became even softer: "Elder sister has misunderstood... Younger sister truly is just worried about her. Well then, if elder sister is unwilling to go to the side hall, how about letting my maid accompany elder sister to the changing room? It's close to the banquet, so changing will be quicker..."

She spoke earnestly, but a trace of calculation flashed in the depths of her eyes.

The side hall was a trap she had meticulously prepared, but the changing room... she had also arranged a backup plan.

No matter what, Su Yaoyao had to "meet with disaster" today!

Watching Su Yun'er’s act of feigned innocence, Su Yaoyao suddenly smiled.

"Alright," she readily agreed.

"Then I'll trouble little sister."

A flash of joy crossed Su Yun'er's heart, and she hurriedly signaled her maid.

Understanding, the maid stepped forward to lead the way: "Eldest Miss Su, please follow this servant."

Su Yaoyao gathered her drenched outer robe and followed the maid toward the changing room.

After walking a few steps, she suddenly turned back and smiled slightly at Su Yun'er, who was still standing in place:

"By the way, little sister, the Crown Prince gave me something just now, telling me to keep it safe."

She retrieved the hair-pin wrapped in sandalwood Buddhist prayer beads from her sleeve and shook it under the moonlight.

The jade and sandalwood complemented each other, radiating brilliant colors.

Of course, she had picked this up while everyone wasn't paying attention, but she wouldn't say that.

"Little sister, do you think... this means His Highness looks at me... differently?"

Without waiting to see Su Yun'er’s instantly distorted expression, she turned and walked away gracefully.

Su Yun'er stared fixedly at her retreating back, her fingernails digging deep into her palms.

The Crown Prince... actually gave her Buddhist beads?!

How could that be!

That cold, otherworldly Crown Prince, how could he look differently at a good-for-nothing like Su Yaoyao?!

No... impossible!

That bitch must be lying!

Su Yun'er forced herself to calm down.

It didn't matter... even if the Crown Prince really paid her some attention, so what?

After tonight, when she became a tainted flower, let's see which man would ever look at her twice!

She turned and walked briskly back toward the banquet, a malicious curve on her lips.

She had to go keep an eye on the Second Prince and make sure he didn't discover any anomalies...

The changing room was on the east side of the imperial garden, an independent chamber.

The maid led Su Yaoyao to the door and stopped: "Eldest Miss Su, please enter. Clean clothes have already been prepared behind the screen. This servant will keep watch outside."

Su Yaoyao pushed the door open and entered.

The room was lit with lamps and sparsely furnished. Behind the screen, a set of light purple garments was indeed placed there, ordinary fabric, ordinary style.

She scanned the room, her gaze landing on the incense burner.

Blue smoke curled from the burner, emanating a sweet, cloying fragrance.

Aphrodisiac.

Su Yaoyao’s lips hooked slightly.

Su Yun'er was really...

So cliché! Couldn't she come up with some fresh moves?

Playing these outdated tricks with these ancients was truly exhausting!

She walked to the window and gently pushed it open a crack.

The night breeze poured in, blowing away some of the sweet, cloying scent.

Behind a corridor pillar, a stealthy figure could vaguely be seen lurking and peeking in this direction.

It was a man.

Su Yun'er was truly... ruthless enough.

Not only did she want to ruin her reputation, but she also wanted to completely cut off all her paths of retreat.

If she were to "meet secretly" with an estranged man here and get caught today, never mind the Crown Prince, even scum like the Second Prince would never want her again.

She might even... lose her life.

Su Yaoyao acted as if she hadn't seen anything.

She walked back to the center of the hall and leisurely untied her drenched outer robe.

The flowing silk slipped down her shoulders, piling at her feet.

Then came her undergarments.

One piece, then another.

The drenched garments were casually discarded on the floor, emitting a soft rustling sound.

Outside the hall, the dark figure seemed unable to hold back any longer, beginning to move quietly toward the door.

With her back to the door, Su Yaoyao listened to the subtle footsteps, the smile at the corners of her lips turning increasingly icy.

The person she was waiting for... was certainly not trash like this.

Just as the dark figure was about to push the door open...

"Thud!"

A muffled sound.

Followed by the sound of a heavy object hitting the ground.

Lingfeng’s lowered voice came from outside the door: "Your Highness, it's aphrodisiac incense, and... he's been drugged with aphrodisiacs."

Then came another voice, as cool and clear as jade:

"Guard it."

The door was pushed open.

The night breeze carrying a faint scent of sandalwood poured into the hall.

Su Yaoyao had already stripped down to a pale-purple dudou (halter bodice) and matching inner trousers.

Moonlight spilled over her, outlining breathtaking curves.

Her waist was slender, no more than a graspable span. Below were full, upturned buttocks, and above... was the fullness of softness almost bursting through the dudou.

Her skin was as white and flawless as mutton-fat jade, casting a pearlescent luster under the moonlight.

Like a jade-carved beauty, fragile yet breathtakingly stunning.

Xiao Chengyuan stood at the doorway, his gaze pausing imperceptibly as it landed on her back.

Yet he quickly averted his eyes, his voice remaining calm and wave-less:

"Miss Su, are you injured?"

Only then did Su Yaoyao slowly turn around, instinctively crossing her hands over her chest in simulated panic...

This action only made the full curve appear even more breathtakingly pronounced.

The suet-jade pendant swayed between the cleavage, emitting a lustrous glow under the dim candlelight.

chapters.title: Cousin... they didn't bring me my undergarment
chapters.content:
Her cheeks bore an unnatural flush, waterdrops still hung on her eyelashes, but her gaze remained as clear as ever.

"Thank you for your concern, Your Highness," she spoke softly, her voice carrying just the right measure of panic and gratitude. "This subject is unharmed. It's just..."

She bit her lip, her long lashes fluttering slightly.

"Just now, in that censer... there seemed to be something amiss. This subject feels... somewhat dizzy."

As she spoke, her body swayed, as if she could no longer stand steadily.

Xiao Chenyuan's brows furrowed slightly.

Naturally, he had also smelled that the incense was problematic. Aphrodisiac incense combined with a numbing agent, their medicinal properties compounding...

He walked briskly to the censer, flicked his sleeve, and the fire in the furnace instantly died out.

"Lingfeng, open the window."

"Yes!"

The night wind poured in, quickly scattering the sweet, cloying scent inside the hall.

Su Yaoyao leaned against the screen, watching Xiao Chenyuan's decisive movements, a flicker of a smile flashing in the depths of her eyes.

It worked, just as expected.

She knew it; that letter from the Grand Tutor's estate wouldn't have been written in vain.

In the letter, her maternal grandfather had described her as "timid, weak, and easily bullied," earnestly imploring His Royal Highness the Crown Prince to offer her extra care and protection.

Given Xiao Chenyuan's character, which deeply respected teachers and valued righteousness, since he had promised, he would never sit idly by.

What was more... earlier outside the hall, he had deliberately warned her about the aphrodisiac incense.

This indicated that he had been watching from the shadows all along.

Therefore, she had dared to gamble, gambling that he would follow, gambling that he would intervene.

Only...

Su Yaoyao lowered her head and looked at her soaked, nearly transparent undergarment.

This method of "care and protection" turned out to be unexpectedly... direct.

"Miss Su." Xiao Chenyuan finished dealing with the censer, turned to look at her, and said,

"This place is no place to linger. I will have a palace maid bring new clothes over, you..."

His words trailed off.

Because Su Yaoyao had suddenly raised her eyes to look at him.

Those eyes were shimmering with moisture, whether from the water vapor or the effects of the medicine, it was unclear.

The corners of her eyes were slightly red, and as her gaze shifted, there was a heart-stopping allure to it.

"Cousin..."

She called out to him softly, her voice as tender as a feather brushing against the tip of the heart, "I... can no longer stand steadily."

As she spoke, her body softened, and she truly began to fall forward.

Xiao Chenyuan extended his hand almost by instinct.

Warm fragrance and soft jade entered his arms.

Her body was very light, yet unimaginably soft.

Beneath her drenched garments, her body temperature was running high, and through the thin fabric, the undulating curves of her figure could be clearly felt.

There was also that scent, a mixture of a maiden's natural fragrance and a faint trace of wine.

Xiao Chenyuan's body stiffened. He was the Empress's adopted son, and her calling him cousin was entirely proper, but still...

He wanted to push her away, but her hands had tightly grasped his sleeves.

"Cousin..."

Su Yaoyao lifted her face to look at him, her eyes full of reliance and helplessness, "Outside... is there still someone? This subject is afraid..."

Her voice was trembling.

It was not an act.

Although the numbing agent's effect was not heavy, she had already been exposed to the aphrodisiac incense, and now, stimulated by the cool sandalwood fragrance radiating from Xiao Chenyuan, the restless heat within her body showed signs of a resurgence.

Xiao Chenyuan lowered his gaze, looking at her flushed cheeks and misty eyes, his brows furrowing even deeper.

"There is no one left."

His voice softened a fraction, a rarity for him. "With me here, no one dares to harm you."

As he spoke, he intended to help her to the couch to sit down.

Yet Su Yaoyao seemed not to hear, shrinking her entire body further into his arms.

Her soaked undergarment brushed against the lapels of his robe, leaving dark water stains behind.

Xiao Chenyuan's breathing paused briefly.

Having studied Buddhism for many years, he had always considered his self-control to be extraordinary.

Yet the warmth and softness in his arms at this moment, the fragrance lingering at the tip of his nose, and her unconscious closeness...

All felt like a silent test.

"Miss Su," his voice deepened by a fraction. "Sit down first; I will go call a palace maid."

"Don't..."

Su Yaoyao shook her head, her fingers tightening their grip on his sleeve. "Don't leave..."

She lifted her face, looking at him with hazy eyes, and suddenly asked softly,

"Your Highness... where are your Buddhist prayer beads?"

Xiao Chenyuan was taken aback.

As she spoke, she actually reached out to touch his wrist, "Why aren't you wearing them?"

Her fingertips were slightly cool. The moment they brushed against the skin of his wrist, Xiao Chenyuan abruptly withdrew his hand.

The movement was somewhat rushed, causing Su Yaoyao to stumble and nearly fall.

Involuntarily, Xiao Chenyuan reached out to steady her once more.

With this back and forth, the distance between the two of them closed even further.

Close enough for him to see the fine droplets of water on her long lashes, close enough to feel her warm breath brush against the side of his neck.

Leaning in his arms, Su Yaoyao suddenly smiled.

That smile carried the seductiveness brought forth by the medicine, yet her gaze cleared for a fleeting second:

"Your Highness... your heart is beating so fast."

Xiao Chenyuan's gaze darkened.

Hesitating no longer, he let go of her, turned to pick up the set of new clothes from the couch, and pressed them into her arms.

"Put them on."

His tone returned to its customary coolness, but upon closer listening, there was a trace of a tightly wound tension that was hard to conceal.

Clutching the garments, Su Yaoyao watched the rare display of panic on his face, the smile in the depths of her eyes deepening.

Yet she knew when enough was then.

"Then..." She bit her lip, her expression innocent,

"Can cousin... turn around?"

Xiao Chenyuan glanced at her and silently turned around.

From behind him came the rustling sound of clothing being put on.

The fabric brushed against skin, occasionally mixed with her suppressed murmurs, likely because the effects of the medicine had not worn off, making her movements somewhat difficult.

Every single sound caused Xiao Chenyuan to speed up the pace at which he twirled his fingertips.

After an unknown length of time, Su Yaoyao's hesitant voice sounded from behind him:

"Cousin..."

"Hmm?"

"Well..." Her voice grew smaller, carrying a sense of embarrassment,

"They... didn't seem to bring me my undergarment..."

Xiao Chenyuan's fingers stopped their movement.

Silence fell within the hall.

Only the crackle and pop of the candle flames could be heard.

After a long moment, Xiao Chenyuan finally spoke, his voice devoid of emotion:

"I will have a palace maid..."

"But to call someone now..." Su Yaoyao interrupted him, her voice dropping lower still, laden with distress,

"If someone were to see Your Highness here... my reputation..."

She left the rest unsaid, but the implication was glaringly obvious.

An unmarried man and woman, alone in a room in the deep of night.

If someone were brought in right now and saw the Crown Prince present here, her reputation would truly be ruined.

Xiao Chenyuan fell silent.

He knew she was right.

However...

"Then what does Miss Su propose?"

Su Yaoyao poked half her body out from behind the screen.

She had already put on the outer robe, the moon-white dress making her skin look as flawless as jade.

Only the collar was slightly open, faintly revealing the empty space beneath.

Her long wet hair draped over her shoulders, and water droplets rolled down, sinking deep into the lapel of her garment.

Her cheeks were still flushed, but her eyes were much clearer, looking at him with an eager expression:

"Your Highness... could you..."

She paused, as if gathering all her courage, before speaking softly:

"Lend this subject one..."

Under the candlelight, her gaze was pure, her tone innocent.

She seemed truly to be a helpless person making a desperate request.

Yet Xiao Chenyuan caught a flash of cunning light darting across the depths of her eyes.

Like a little fox whose scheme had succeeded.

He quietly watched her for a moment.

Suddenly, he raised his hand and unbuttoned his outer robe.

The moon-white outer garment slipped away, revealing the plain white inner robe underneath.

He handed the outer robe to her, his voice calm:

"Wear this."

Su Yaoyao took the outer robe, which still retained his body heat, and blinked:

"Then Your Highness..."

"I have matters to attend to." Xiao Chenyuan interrupted her, turned, and walked toward the door.

"In a quarter of an hour, Lingfeng will send palace maids over. Once Miss Su has tidied up, you may return to the banquet."

With those words, he pushed the door open and stepped out.

The night wind poured in, fluttering his thin inner robe.

Clutching the outer robe that still carried the lingering scent of sandalwood, Su Yaoyao watched his cool, solitary silhouette vanish into the night, and slowly the corners of her lips curled upward.

She lowered her head, burying her face into the soft fabric.

She took a deep breath.

The sandalwood was crisp and cold, mingled with a trace of his uniquely icy aura.

"He runs really fast..."

She murmured softly, the smile in her eyes swirling.

"However..."

"There is plenty of time ahead, Your Highness the Crown Prince."

Cold and ascetic?

Hah.

She would make it a point to see what this iceberg looked like when it melted.

chapters.title: Let this Prince pamper you properly...
chapters.content:
Clutching the outer robe that still retained the scent of sandalwood, Su Yaoyao hadn't even had the chance to savor this "trophy" when the door of the side hall was lightly knocked upon.

"Miss Su."

It was a palace maid's voice. "This maid, by order of His Royal Highness the Crown Prince, has come to wait upon you."

Such high efficiency.

Su Yaoyao carefully folded the moon-white outer robe, hid it inside the bundle containing her new clothes, and then responded, "Come in."

The door opened, and a neatly featured palace maid walked in with lowered head, holding a complete set of clothes, from inner garments to outer robes, everything was provided.

"After the young lady has changed, please follow this maid to the Sinyin Pavilion." The maid's voice was respectful. "Her Majesty the Empress is waiting for you there."

Su Yaoyao raised an eyebrow.

Sinyin Pavilion? That was a secluded courtyard not far from the banquet area.

It seemed her maternal aunt did not want people to know about this private meeting.

"Thank you for the trouble." Su Yaoyao smiled, holding the clothes, and turned behind the screen.

Behind the screen, as Su Yaoyao changed her clothes, her mind raced.

For the Empress to summon her alone at a time like this was by no means simple.

The Empress should have already discerned clues from what happened at the banquet earlier.

Added to Xiao Chenyuan's uncharacteristic intervention...

This maternal aunt of hers was probably losing her composure.

She just wondered how far this aunt of hers was willing to go for her sake.

---

Back at the banquet, the silk and bamboo music played on, goblets intersecting.

Yet the minds of quite a few were no longer on the singing, dancing, or fine wine.

Su Wan'er fidgeted anxiously with her wine cup, her gaze frequently drifting toward the outside of the hall.

Why wasn't there any movement yet?

The man she had arranged should have succeeded by now.

Even if Su Yaoyao had managed to escape by luck, there should have been some sort of commotion...

Yet the side hall remained dead silent.

Just as she was growing frantic, she suddenly saw the Empress's head palace maid step close to the Empress's ear and whisper a few words.

The Empress's expression changed imperceptibly, and she immediately stood up, announced to everyone that she felt a bit fatigued and was going to change her clothes, and left the banquet with her retinue.

Su Wan'er's heart skipped a beat.

The Empress had gone too?!

Could it be... things had blown up? Was the Empress going to clean up the mess for Su Yaoyao?

No!

If the Empress intended to shield her and sweep the matter under the rug, wouldn't all her efforts today be for nothing?!

No!

She had gone to such great lengths to set this trap; she absolutely could not let Su Yaoyao have a chance at a comeback!

Su Wan'er bit her lip and cast her gaze not far away, where the Second Prince, Xiao Qiming, was drinking and laughing with others.

Taking a deep breath, she put on a tearful expression and walked over.

"Your Highness..." She gently tugged at Xiao Qiming's sleeve.

Xiao Qiming turned back, saw her red-rimmed eyes, and frowned, "What is it?"

"I-I'm worried about Elder Sister..." Su Wan'er said with a crying lilt in her voice. "Elder Sister went to change her clothes and hasn't returned for nearly half an hour. Just now... just now I seemed to see a man heading toward the side hall..."

Xiao Qiming's expression darkened. "What?"

"I-I don't know if I saw wrong..." Su Wan'er said timidly, "But Elder Sister hasn't returned for so long, and I'm afraid something might have happened to her... Your Highness, should we go take a look?"

Xiao Qiming had already been harboring lingering resentment over Su Yaoyao's "abnormality" today, and hearing Su Wan'er say this now instantly flared his temper.

That shameless woman! Could she really have dared to meet a man in secret during the imperial banquet?!

"Let's go!" He grabbed Su Wan'er's hand, "This Prince wants to see what kind of game she's playing!"

The two left the banquet together without drawing too much attention.

After all, the Second Prince's favoritism toward the Su family's concubine-born daughter was long no secret.

Outside the side hall, all was quiet.

The door was ajar, and no lights were lit inside.

Su Wan'er felt a surge of wild elation; it was so quiet, she must have succeeded! After getting what he wanted, that man was probably...

"Your Highness, the door isn't closed..." she whispered a reminder.

With a pale, iron-clad expression, Xiao Qiming raised his foot and kicked the door open with a loud bang!

Scattered across the floor were several pieces of women's clothing, shimmering brocade, precisely the outfit Su Yaoyao had worn today.

The screen had crashed to the ground, and most of the water in the bathing tub had spilled out.

Total chaos.

Yet... there was not a single soul inside.

Su Wan'er froze.

Where were the people?

Where was the man she had arranged?! Where was Su Yaoyao?!

"Su Yaoyao!" Xiao Qiming roared furiously, "Get your ass out here!"

No one answered.

Only the night wind sweeping through the open window caused the curtains to sway gently.

Reluctant to give up, Su Wan'er walked further inside.

She refused to believe it! How could people just vanish?!

Could it be... Su Yaoyao had sensed something was wrong and fled?

Or had that man failed in his task?

She failed to notice that the door behind them had been gently pushed shut by the night wind.

Nor did she notice that the gilded censer in the corner, which had already burned out, had somehow begun to drift with wisps of blue smoke once more.

Su Wan'er suddenly felt a wave of dizziness.

Standing by the door, Xiao Qiming suddenly felt a surge of heat.

Tugging at his collar, his tone grew increasingly impatient, "Su Wan'er, what on earth did you come to see? There's no one here..."

Before his voice died away, his gaze suddenly locked.

Next to that pile of wet clothes on the floor lay a lotus-pink undergarment.

Very thin, very sheer.

Having been soaked in water, the twin-lotus embroidery pattern upon it was faintly visible.

Xiao Qiming's Adam's apple bobbed.

He suddenly recalled how Su Yaoyao's drenched clothes had clung tightly to her figure back at the banquet.

Those curves... were breathtaking.

And those eyes, filled with tears yet shining astonishingly bright when she lifted her face to look at him.

Why hadn't he noticed before... that good-for-nothing actually...

"Your Highness?" Su Wan'er turned her head, and seeing him standing frozen in place, she called out in confusion.

Yet when she saw Xiao Qiming's expression, her heart plummeted.

His face... why was it so red?

His gaze didn't look right either...

"Your Highness, are you feeling unwell?" Su Wan'er quickly stepped forward, wanting to help him out.

But the moment her hand touched Xiao Qiming's arm, he grabbed it back with a reverse grip.

His grip was fierce, squeezing her wrist until it hurt.

"Y-Your Highness?" Su Wan'er panicked.

Staring at her with hazy eyes and heavy breathing, Xiao Qiming muttered, "Wan'er... you look... so pretty today..."

"What are you saying, Your Highness..." Su Wan'er tried to pull her hand back, only to find herself grasped even tighter.

The sweet, cloying fragrance grew stronger and stronger.

Su Wan'er also gradually began to feel dizzy, a strange, unfamiliar heat rising from the depths of her body.

A sudden realization struck her; this was the numbing aphrodisiac she had arranged for others to use! How could it be...

It was already too late.

Xiao Qiming had already consumed a fair amount of wine, and now, stimulated by this sweet, cloying fragrance, he felt a wave of feverish heat surge up from his lower abdomen.

He pulled her directly into his arms, his scorching breath panting against the side of her neck:

"Wan'er... let this Prince pamper you properly..."

"No... Your Highness... you mustn't..." Su Wan'er resisted in a panic, but her strength waned as her body grew increasingly limp.

Amidst her blurring consciousness, she heard the sound of fabric tearing.

And the faint click of the door being quietly locked from the outside.

chapters.title: Flirting by Imperial Decree
chapters.content:
Inside the Qingyin Pavilion, candlelight burned brightly.

The Empress sat in the seat of honor, holding a teacup, her gaze fixed on Su Yaoyao below.

This niece of hers had given her too many surprises today.

At the imperial banquet, that act of retreating to advance, looking pitiful and delicate, had already made her view the girl in a new light.

And just now, the wet nurse had reported that the Crown Prince himself had gone to the side hall and resolved the trouble there...

A deep glint flashed in the Empress's eyes.

She dismissed her attendants, leaving only Su Yaoyao behind.

"What do you make of today's events?" the Empress asked, her tone devoid of emotion.

Su Yaoyao lowered her eyes. "Replying to Your Majesty, someone wants to harm this subject's daughter."

"Do you know who?"

"I have an idea in mind." Su Yaoyao raised her eyes to look at the Empress. "Only, there is no proof."

The Empress smiled.

That smile carried a hint of approval and a dash of calculation.

The Empress took her hand, leading her over to sit beside her.

"You have been wronged." The Empress gently patted the back of Su Yaoyao's hand, her tone laden with pity. "Such despicable tricks, and they dared to use them at an imperial banquet. Rest assured, Aunt will give you an explanation."

"Thank you, Aunt, for your care." Su Yaoyao lowered her gaze, her voice soft. "Yaoyao is not wronged, it's just... that I have brought trouble to Aunt."

"Silly child, what talk of trouble or no trouble." The Empress watched her submissive appearance, satisfaction flashing in her eyes. "You are the only bloodline left by my sister. If Aunt doesn't care for you, who will?"

She paused, turning the conversation: "It's just Yaoyao, you have seen it too. This palace... has never been peaceful. Today it's a dancing girl drugging you, tomorrow who knows what it will be. As a young lady with no backing, you will suffer in the end."

Su Yaoyao raised her eyes, her gaze clear. "Aunt means..."

She paused, shifting the focus: "As for the Crown Prince... what do you think of him?"

Finally, it was here.

Su Yaoyao understood in her heart, but appropriately revealed a trace of bashfulness on her face. "His Highness the Crown Prince... is aloof and otherworldly, this subject's daughter wouldn't dare to speak presumptuously."

"Aloof is aloof, but he is a man after all."

The Empress patted the back of her hand, lowering her voice somewhat. "Yaoyao, you are a clever child. You should know why Aunt wants you to get close to the Crown Prince."

"Though the Crown Prince is raised under my name, he is not my biological son. All these years, he has been devoted to Buddhist scriptures and kept away from women, leaving the Eastern Palace vacant to this day. Although His Majesty hasn't said anything, there are already murmurs at court, how can a Crown Prince who refuses to marry and have children inherit the grand mandate?"

Su Yaoyao listened quietly, understanding in her heart.

"And you are different." The Empress looked at her, her gaze sharp.

"You are the Grand Preceptor's granddaughter and my own niece; your status is sufficient. More importantly... today the Crown Prince seemed somewhat different toward you."

Su Yaoyao appropriately lowered her head, revealing a shy expression. "His Highness... was merely pitying this subject's daughter for being bullied."

"Pity or something else." The Empress patted her hand. "Yaoyao, as long as you catch the Crown Prince's eye and conceive his heir, the position of Crown Princess... and even the future, will all be yours."

She stroked Su Yaoyao's hand, giving it a gentle pat.

"Only when the Crown Prince's position is secure can my position and Yi'er's position be secure. And Yi'er is young and frail... How many eyes in this inner court and outer court are watching?" The Empress sighed, weariness flashing in her eyes.

"Imperial Noble Consort Chen has been making frequent moves lately, and your father is a fence-sitter. If the Second Prince truly gains power, none of us will have an easy time."

Su Yaoyao raised her eyes, looking at the undisguised calculation and anxiety in the Empress's eyes, and sneered inwardly.

Indeed, in the face of power, any familial affection was hollow.

This aunt of hers only thought of her as a niece now that she had utility value.

However... perfect.

It was just a mutual exchange of needs.

"Aunt, rest assured." Su Yaoyao bloomed with a submissive smile. "Yaoyao knows what to do."

The Empress nodded with satisfaction. "Good child. However..."

Her brows furrowed slightly. "The Second Prince's side is ultimately a trouble. Your engagement was bestowed by His Majesty personally. To dissolve it, unless..."

Before she finished speaking, urgent footsteps suddenly sounded outside the hall.

Followed by the head maid's panicked voice:

"Your Majesty! This is bad! Over at the side hall... something has happened!"

The Empress's expression sank. "What happened? Speak clearly!"

"It's, it's the Second Prince... and the Su family's second young miss..." The maid's voice was trembling. "They were found... together... disheveled..."

"What?!" The Empress abruptly stood up.

Su Yaoyao also rose, her face appropriately showing shock and heartache.

Yet within her lowered eyes, a knowing smile flashed by.

The Empress hurried toward the door, taking a few steps before turning back. "Yaoyao, you..."

"Aunt, go ahead." Su Yaoyao said softly. "This subject's daughter... this subject's daughter will be right behind."

The Empress seemed to understand something. She glanced at Su Yaoyao, appreciation flashing in the depths of her eyes.

Then she hurried away with her entourage.

The hall returned to silence.

Su Yaoyao walked to the window and pushed open half of it.

The night wind surged in, stirring the stray hairs at her cheek.

She gazed in the direction of the side hall, where the murmurs of a crowd could already be faintly heard.

A cold arc slowly formed at the corners of her lips.

"Aunt need not worry..."

She whispered to herself, her fingertips brushing the swaying Buddhist prayer beads at her ear:

"Look, isn't there a 'good show' to watch now?"

"As for the engagement..."

She turned around, looking at herself in the mirror, eyes rippling, smiling brightly.

"Soon... it won't be a problem anymore."
